For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
papers.abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.

papers.title: A Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem for marked graphs
papers.abstract: The classical Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem characterizes graphs with least eigenvalue at least $-2$ in terms of generalized line graphs, exceptional graphs, and root systems. In this paper, we establish a marked graph extension of this theorem. For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and a binary vector $\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^n$, we completely characterize all marked graphs $\mathbf{G}=(G,\mathbf{b})$ such that $λ_{\min}(A(G)+\mathbf{b}\mathbf{b}^\top-J_n)\ge -2$, where $J_n$ denotes the all-ones matrix of order $n$. Using representations by finite root systems, we show that every irreducible marked graph satisfying the above inequality is represented by either the root system $B_n$ or the exceptional root system $E_8$. This leads to a complete structural characterization in terms of irreducible marked graphs, namely induced subgraphs of extended generalized line graphs, the marked graph $(2K_1,\mathbf{0})$, and exceptional graphs with all vertices marked. In the special case $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{j}$, our characterization reduces to the original Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem. The root system $B_n$ and extended generalized line graphs play the roles occupied by $D_n$ and generalized line graphs in the classical theory. We further apply the characterization to graphs whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$, showing that every $-2$-markable graph satisfies this spectral condition.

papers.title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
papers.abstract: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $γ_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
papers.abstract: We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). Then, each server answers a PIR query in time $T_s(n)$, by reading at most $T_s$ bits of its data structure and sending them to the user. In the two server setting ($s=2$), our PIR protocols achieve $T_2 = n^{0.82}$, matching the server time of the state-of-the-art schemes of Henzinger and Ragavan (EUROCRYPT 2026) while shrinking their storage from $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ to $n+1$ bits. With $s \geq 3$ servers, our PIR protocols retain the $n+1$ bits of storage and additionally improve on the server time of all prior information-theoretic $s$-server schemes with $n^{1+o(1)}$ storage: for example, achieving $T_3 = n^{0.74}$ and $T_{10} = n^{0.61}$ (previously $n^{0.79}$ and $n^{0.75}$). Asymptotically, as the server count $s$ grows, we shrink the number of servers required to achieve a given server-work exponent from $s^{3.9}$ to $s$. Our results draw inspiration from matching-vector techniques (Efremenko, STOC 2009), which we generalize to handle degree-two computations in the exponent. Using this generalization, we build doubly-efficient PIR from the new intermediate abstraction of Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions. Then, we construct such Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via a connection to modular forms and complex analysis: if a Fourier-sparse cone-delta function does not exist, then there exists a modular form which has too many roots, contradicting the valence formula.

papers.title: Rotational Encoding of Objective Functions for Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Angular Rotational Counter (ARC), a novel approach to represent objective functions that can be decomposed as a weighted sum of Boolean functions. ARC encodes the objective as an accumulated sum of quantum rotations onto a single-qubit register instead of a multi-qubit register used in much of the previous literature. We mathematically establish and experimentally validate that these rotations sum to the objective value for all possible solutions and derive the relationship between the resulting measurement probabilities and the objective. This design was applied to construct a quantum oracle for the state assignment problem of finite automata and state machines using a weighted Hamming distance cost function, which is a special case of the quadratic assignment problem. We evaluate this oracle design on 26 benchmarks and compare it with corresponding Boolean-based oracles on four cost metrics. Across these benchmarks, the oracle with ARC produces a mean reduction in the qubit count of 20.8%, gate count of 89.3%, circuit depth of 92.4%, and quantum cost of 90.6%. These results demonstrate substantial reductions in circuit cost for the evaluated benchmarks and establish rotational encoding as a promising approach for representing objective functions in optimization based on quantum search algorithms.

papers.title: An operator theoretical approach to weak solvability of a porous medium equation with Neumann boundary condition
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the Neumann problem for the porous medium equation, \[ u_t - Δa(u) = f \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\times (0, T), \qquad \nabla a(u) \cdot ν=0 \quad \mbox{on}\ \partial Ω\times (0, T), \qquad u(\cdot, 0) = u_0 \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\] in a smoothly bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ $(N \in \mathbb{N})$, where $T \in (0,\infty)$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial Ω$, and where $f$ and $u_0$ are given. A typical example in mind is $a(u)=|u|^{p-2}u$ with $p \in [2, \infty)$. The main interest is weak solvability of the problem in the case that $u_0 \in H^1(Ω)^*$, $f \in L^2(0,T; H^1(Ω)^*)$. Under the condition that the mean value of $f(t)$ vanishes for almost all $t \in (0,T)$, existence of weak solutions is established by an application of abstract results from operator theory, for instance, properties of Gâteaux derivative. The key of the proof lies in the approximate equation \[ [(\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} u_\varepsilon]_t + a(u_\varepsilon) = (\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} f, \quad \varepsilon \in (0,1), \] where the map $\varepsilon I - Δ$ from $H^1(Ω)$ onto its dual space is regarded as the Riesz isomorphism of $H^1(Ω)$ equipped with an appropriate topology.

papers.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

papers.title: AI and Mathematical Work on Mastodon: Attention, Topics, and Target-Specific Evaluations
papers.abstract: How does a mathematical community discuss AI on a federated social platform? We study 24,920 public posts from January--September 2026 by 272 accounts in a fixed roster of 1,002 Mastodon accounts whose profiles indicate mathematical research or study. LLM-assisted extraction identifies 1,191 AI-for-mathematics posts by 101 accounts. Their share of all posts rises from 1.1\% in January to 11.5\% in September, with contributing accounts increasing from 10 to 59. We represent discussion through linked target--aspect--stance triples, separating what is discussed from the property assessed and the author's evaluation. From July to September, capability and usefulness decline as a share of related discussion, while social and institutional concerns increase; changing contributors account for much of the latter shift. Among 38 accounts evaluating both technical quality or utility and communication, credit, or verification procedures, the procedural negative-component fraction is 19.4 percentage points higher on average (95\% account-bootstrap interval: 3.8--35.1). Matching targets within posts gives a similar direction. Repeated extraction varies substantially at the level of individual triples, although replacing the repeated sample preserves the aggregate contrast. Around OpenAI's October 6 mathematics release, related-post share rises from 9.6\% to 13.6\%, and contributing accounts increase from 13 to 28. Post-release discussion includes appreciation of the results' potential mathematical value and applications alongside criticism of promotion centered on result counts, limited methodological disclosure, and verification arrangements.

papers.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
papers.abstract: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.

papers.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
papers.abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.

papers.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory
papers.abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.

papers.title: When Should AI Overturn a Human Decision? Controversy at the 2026 World Cup and a $\sqrt{2/π}$ Solution
papers.abstract: We study how to combine a human binary call (a referee's offside or onside decision) with an AI numerical measurement (VAR's estimate of an attacker's position relative to the offside line). We derive an explicit maximum-likelihood rule that determines when the referee's call should stand and when a conflicting VAR measurement should overturn it. Our model treats the true offside margin as fixed and unknown and assumes independent additive Gaussian errors in the human's perception and the AI measurement. When both errors have zero means and known standard deviations $σ_H$ and $σ_{AI}$, respectively, the reversal threshold is $\sqrt{2/π}\,σ^2_{AI}/σ_H$. An onside call is overturned precisely when VAR's measured offside margin exceeds this threshold---not merely because VAR places the attacker beyond the offside line. We also derive the rule when either source has a systematic bias. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimate of the true margin exists and is unique, while the final binary decision requires only a threshold comparison, without computing that estimate numerically. We illustrate the rule through numerical examples and show how to estimate the error parameters from calibration data. The same analysis applies beyond soccer to binary classification problems in which a human call and an AI measurement satisfy the stated model. This paper is intended for educational purposes: we aim to illustrate how undergraduate students and advanced high school students familiar with basic probability and calculus can investigate research questions in AI and its applications.

papers.title: On the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension
papers.abstract: We study the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension in dimension $1+d$. For fixed positive surface tension, we establish local well-posedness for arbitrary initial interfaces in $H^{s+1}$ and density perturbations in $H^s$, with $s>(d+3)/2$. When $s>(d+5)/2$, we justify the local vanishing-surface-tension limit for stable interfaces and sufficiently small density perturbations. In a finite-depth strip over $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat bottom and fixed positive surface tension, we prove global well-posedness and uniform anisotropic energy bounds for small compatible perturbations of an equilibrium with strictly stable stratification, under a horizontal low-frequency condition.

papers.title: The minimum forcing number of graphs and involutory weighted adjacency matrices
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with a perfect matching. The minimum forcing number $f(G)$ of $G$ is the smallest size of a matching in $G$ that is contained in exactly one perfect matching. For the $d$-hypercube $Q_d$ ($d\geq 2$) Diwan (2019) determined $f(Q_d)=2^{d-2}$ by using a linear algebraic method, and Mohammadian (2022) generalized this method and showed that $f(G\square K_2)=n/2$ when a bipartite graph $G$ admits order $n$ and an involutory weighted adjacency matrix over a field $\mathbb F$, where $\square$ denotes the Cartesian product. In this paper, we further prove that if $\operatorname{char}\mathbb{F}\neq 2$, then $\frac{n}{2}\le f(G\mathbin{\square} P_k)\le \frac{n}{2}\lceil\frac{k}{2}\rceil$ for every $k\ge 2$, where $P_k$ is the $k$-vertex path; this recovers Mohammadian's result when $k=2$, and the lower bound is attained for $k=3$. Moreover, we extend this method to non-bipartite graphs. Recursively constructing the adjacency matrix of the folded hypercube $FQ_n$ over the binary field $\mathbb F_2$, we prove that $f(FQ_n\mathbin{\square} K_2)=2^{n-1}$ for every even $n$. Combined with Mohammadian's result for odd $n$, this establishes the same formula for all $n\geq 1$.

papers.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
papers.abstract: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast. Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity complement the theory, illustrating the roles of internal-variable dimension and sample complexity in learning homogenized responses from unit-cell data. Theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Curvature estimates for shrinking gradient Ricci solitons
papers.abstract: Suppose $(M^5,g,f)$ is a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with bounded scalar curvature. We prove that if $ν(g)>-\log 2$, then its Riemannian curvature is bounded. The proof uses curvature blow-up, a local Ricci estimate, and the splitting given by the rescaled potential. An entropy estimate then allows us to apply the volume-ratio gap theorem for Ricci-flat four-manifolds.

papers.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=π^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $σ$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schrödinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.

papers.title: Structure-Informed Electromagnetic Feedback Control of the Vlasov-Maxwell System with Delayed Observations
papers.abstract: Feedback control of kinetic plasma instabilities is challenging because observing the full phase-space distribution is costly, while sensing and actuation inevitably introduce delay. We develop a structure-informed electromagnetic feedback framework for the Vlasov-Maxwell system that uses only macroscopic observations to control the full kinetic distribution. We first show that magnetic actuation alone does not directly regulate radial velocity moments, motivating the use of combined electric and magnetic controls. A nonlinear perturbation estimate yields an instantaneous cancellation-dissipation feedback law. To account for delayed observations, we then use Maxwell's equations to identify the macroscopic quantities governing the resulting cancellation errors, namely currents and spatial field gradients. These quantities serve as inputs to a low-rank neural operator that learns a residual correction to the delayed cancellation baseline. Thus, while the feedback depends only on low-dimensional macroscopic observables, the control objective remains the stabilization of the full distribution toward a prescribed kinetic equilibrium. Numerical experiments for two-stream and Weibel-type instabilities demonstrate effective long-time stabilization under substantial feedback delays.

papers.title: On the robustness of locally D-optimal designs under parameter uncertainty in single-factor generalized linear models
papers.abstract: Local and Bayesian approaches to optimal experimental design specify information about the regression parameters through a nominal value and a prior distribution, respectively. A practical question is whether accounting for parameter uncertainty justifies replacing a locally optimal design. We investigate when locally D-optimal designs remain Bayesian D-optimal in single-factor Poisson, gamma and logistic regression on the unit interval. Analytical arguments and numerical comparisons under normal and uniform slope priors examine how prior form and dispersion affect the optimal support and the Bayesian D-efficiency of retaining a local design.

papers.title: Homomesy of tropical $T$-systems for pairs of simply laced Dynkin diagrams
papers.abstract: For a pair of simply laced Dynking diagrams $X$ and $X'$, we prove Chin's homomesy conjecture on the number of red and blue mutations in a period of the tropical Zamolodchikov $T$-system associated to $(X, X')$ using Nakanishi's dilogarithm identity.

papers.title: Nonexistence of cusp singularities for gravity waves of extreme form
papers.abstract: In this paper we revisit the geometric approach developed by Vărvărucă and Weiss for the Stokes conjecture for gravity water waves near stagnation points, in both the irrotational and rotational settings. They introduced monotonicity formulas and frequency formulas to classify all possible singularities of solutions at stagnation points. Two questions were left open: 1. whether cusp singularities can be excluded in higher dimensions $n\geq 3$ [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]; 2. whether cusp singularities for rotational waves can be excluded under the Rayleigh-Taylor condition [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 29 (2012)]. We answer both questions in the affirmative. Our main results show that cusp singularities do not exist in higher dimensions and cannot occur for rotational waves even without assuming the Rayleigh-Taylor condition. Our argument combines a delicate analysis of the weighted volume arising from the corresponding free boundary problem with a weighted isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: A Cheeger-Müller Theorem For Flat Superconnections
papers.abstract: For a flat superconnection ${\mathbb{A}}$ on a ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-graded vector bundle $E$ over a closed oriented odd-dimensional manifold $M$, we prove a Cheeger-Müller type theorem as proposed by Arias Abad and Schätz. Namely, that the topological Reidemeister norm of ${\mathbb{A}}$ as defined by them equals the Ray-Singer metric defined by Mathai and Wu. The main step proves an analytic reduction result identified by Arias Abad and Schätz and formulated as a conjecture by the author, that the Ray-Singer metric coincides with that of the fibrewise cohomology $H(E,\partial)$ with its Gauss-Manin connection, where $\partial$ is the component of ${\mathbb{A}}$ of form degree zero, under the Knudsen-Mumford isomorphism associated to the form-degree spectral sequence. As an application, we consider Goette's Morse flat superconnection of a fibrewise Morse function on a fibre bundle with even-dimensional fibres over an oriented odd-dimensional base.

papers.title: A level-set method for shape and topology optimization of Stokes--Darcy flows with Beavers--Joseph--Saffman coupling
papers.abstract: We propose a level-set method for shape and topology optimization of Stokes--Darcy flows with Beavers--Joseph--Saffman interface coupling. We formulate the Stokes--Darcy system with BJS interface conditions using a level-set representation and establish existence and uniqueness of its solution. We further prove existence of minimizers for the viscous-energy minimization and least-squares inverse problems within this framework. Continuous Fréchet differentiability of the control-to-state map is proved, and objective derivatives are derived using an adjoint approach. A reaction--diffusion evolution scheme combined with mixed finite elements is developed to find the optimized interface and accommodate topology changes. Two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments verify the derived sensitivities and demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in minimizing viscous energy dissipation and reconstructing interfaces from partial and noisy velocity observations.

papers.title: Super-resolution quantum imaging via multiphoton correlation
papers.abstract: The resolution of conventional imaging is fundamentally constrained by the diffraction limit. Here we demonstrate that this limit can be overcome using classical thermal light, through the correlation of multiphoton subsystems. By resolving the photon numbers detected in the two arms of a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer, the correlation function exhibits a narrowed peak or dip whose width is tunable via the average photon number. Temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively, are experimentally achieved. As a proof-of-principle experiment, a double-pinhole that is completely unresolved by standard ghost imaging becomes clearly distinguishable via the correlation of two-photon versus zero-photon. The principle of this super-resolution imaging can be interpreted as a combination of classical super-resolution imaging and quantum super-resolution imaging. This work provides a versatile platform for super-resolution imaging and lithography, and opens a new avenue for exploring the boundary between classical and nonclassical phenomena.

papers.title: Nonassociative gradings on infinite-dimensional triangular algebras
papers.abstract: We study group gradings on triangular algebras relative to a well-ordered basis, with multiplication $x\circ_λy=xy+λyx$. For $λ\notin\{0,\pm1\}$, every grading on a finite-dimensional triangular algebra is isomorphic to an elementary grading. In infinite dimension, the same conclusion holds for the algebra of finite-range maps, for the finite-map algebra on a basis of order type $ω$, and for closed gradings on the full triangular algebra. The infinite-dimensional results also hold for $λ=1$ in characteristic different from $2$. For intermediate algebras whose finite-range ideal is graded, we obtain an elementary description relative to a unitriangular basis. The proofs construct neutral associative idempotents with singleton diagonal supports. We also prove that the radical of the full triangular algebra is graded for every nonzero $λ$, and that gradings on the finite-range algebra and closed gradings on the full algebra have finite support under the classification hypotheses.

papers.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
papers.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

papers.title: An asymptotic preserving scheme for kinetic equations describing bacterial traveling pulses
papers.abstract: We consider a kinetic model for bacterial chemotaxis that describes the propagation of traveling pulses driven by a nutrient and a self-produced chemoattractant. In the diffusive regime, the model converges to a macroscopic drift-diffusion system with bounded chemotactic fluxes. We construct a fully discrete asymptotic preserving (AP) finite difference scheme based on a micro-macro decomposition of the kinetic equation. The method is stable uniformly with respect to the scaling parameter and, as this parameter tends to zero, reduces to a consistent discretization of the limiting macroscopic equations. We prove positivity and mass conservation for the limiting scheme, and use a positivity-preserving correction for the kinetic solver. Numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed traveling pulses at both the kinetic and the macroscopic level, validate the theoretical traveling wave speed, and illustrate the convergence of the kinetic model to its macroscopic limit.

papers.title: Proof of the Rényi QNEC
papers.abstract: We give a general proof of the Rényi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.

papers.title: An optimal quantum strategy for the $2$-hat game
papers.abstract: We study the two-player hat game as a two-input, three-output non-local game. We calculate the quantum commuting value and show that it coincides with the quantum one. In particular, we show that \[ω_{\rm q}(H_2)=ω_{\mathrm{qc}}(H_2)=\frac{15+\sqrt{33}}{36}\approx 0.576238.\] We achieve the optimal quantum advantage using a shared non-maximally entangled qutrit state. To establish optimality, we exploit the game's symmetry under the dihedral group $D_8$ and apply its representation theory to substantially reduce the complexity of the underlying matrix problem. We also determine the no-signalling value $ω_{\mathrm{ns}}(H_2)=2/3$.

papers.title: Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps
papers.abstract: Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. For every countable set $P\subset[0,1]$, we prove that the set of points whose orbit closure is disjoint from $P$ is absolute winning on $[0,1]$. Our proof combines a potential game argument with an interval tree constructed from successive returns.

papers.title: Advantage Distillation in Paired-State Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: We investigate advantage distillation for paired-state Loop-Back quantum key distribution, with a fixed optical station serving a lightweight portable terminal. Alice prepares two polarization-encoded pulses, Bob selects and applies a polarization filter to each pulse, and Alice infers his selections from the returned detection pattern. The proposed advantage-distillation step selects consistent blocks of three two-bit records using two independent public parity checks on a minimal connected graph. The closing edge of a parity polygon is shown to be redundant: any spanning tree of the same vertices has the same acceptance set. We derive exact acceptance probabilities, residual-error laws, and retention rates. Under independent bit errors, the three-record filter reduces the leading error term from e to e^2, while its cost in discarded records and public information is accounted for explicitly. A modular security theorem bounds the additional guessing advantage available to an adversary after syndrome disclosure and block acceptance, including arbitrary quantum side information. We also evaluate a specified single-photon passive-tap optical channel, obtaining a positive conditional entropy bound and exact accepted-block security quantities. This parity-based advantage-distillation step detects discrepancies by postselection; it does not correct individual errors and is intended to precede conventional reconciliation. The architecture suggests two further directions: hybrid filtering and reconciliation, and key establishment between portable users accessing a shared quantum station.

papers.title: Becker's Conjecture on Compositions of Higher Degree Diagonal Forms
papers.abstract: Becker's conjecture asserts that a rational composition of sums of $d$-th powers of size $[r,s,n]$, with $d>2$, requires $n \ge rs$. We show that this formulation fails over every characteristic-zero field in odd degree, and in every degree over a suitable finite extension of $\Q$. Over formally real fields in even degree, however, we prove that every polynomial composition satisfies $n\ge rs$.

papers.title: Model-family selection and recovery-gate design in generator-based noise tomography
papers.abstract: Family selection in generator-model noise tomography, usually quoted as a property of the hardware, is a hypothesis test whose shot floor is closed form, $N^{*}=λ_{\mathrm{req}}/(r_{\mathrm{b}} S)^{2}$, controlled by the absolute bias $r_{\mathrm{b}} S$ rather than by the relative residual $r_{\mathrm{b}}$, and therefore computable for any device before a single shot is taken. The same computation prices the recovery gates, because the fingerprint that fixes a family's residual and the Fisher information that ranks the designs are read off the same map: there is no design-independent verdict and no family-independent design optimum. Whether a design can move that price is structural, not numerical: a bias confined to the block every design measures identically is design-blind, while one that reaches the code blocks can be repriced by a factor of sixty-eight. The two platforms here are its extremes, at $98.1\%$ and $48.0\%$ in the design-blind block. At the reference point the floor is $1.1\times10^{7}$ and $6.7\times10^{6}$ shots per component for the two families, so at the $10^{5}$ shots a run spends the test has power $0.053$ at a level of $0.05$ and the residual it reports is shot noise. Rebuilding the fingerprint under each of the sixty-four designs moves the floor by $68$ on one platform and $1.7$ on the other, and the most precise design costs ten times more shots for the verdict than the cheapest to test. All sixty-four placements are full rank, so the design problem is one of conditioning: at three gates the rms varies by factors of $2.7$ and $3.9$ with placement alone, while the optimum over counts is flat. At five qubits the same rule moves the floor by $21$, while the verdict itself costs $10^{9}$ shots; checked against the calibration of a real three-qubit register, the floor is a requirement on systematic control before it is a shot count.

papers.title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.

papers.title: The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem
papers.abstract: We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. In the positive-definite case, we determine the representing measures, prove their uniqueness and specify the admissible endpoint masses. No boundedness assumption on the support or asymptotic conditions on the recurrence coefficients are imposed.

papers.title: Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{ψ,\varphi}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{ψ,\varphi}$ and that of the composition operator $C_\varphi$.

papers.title: The Alt-Phillips Multiple Membrane Free Boundary Problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by diffusion--reaction processes in porous catalysts, we study an Alt--Phillips model for ordered membranes with weighted gap interactions. The model connects adhesive harmonic junctions \cite{DSS24} and forced multiple membranes \cite{SY19} through the exponent $0<γ<1$. For arbitrary positive weights, we prove optimal $C^{1,β-1}$ regularity, where $β=2/(2-γ)$, and obtain nontrivial $β$-homogeneous blowup limits through Weiss almost monotonicity. Under strict discrete concavity of the weights, we establish a gluing principle, minimality of flat single-gap cones, and $C^{1,α}$ free boundary regularity at points admitting such blowups. We also classify all one-dimensional vertically critical cones. For three membranes, we identify cone families that are non-minimizing for small $γ$ and minimizing near $γ=1$.

papers.title: Isoperimetric comparison for surfaces with nonnegative curvature and uniformly convex boundary
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp relative isoperimetric comparison for compact surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature and smooth nonempty boundary whose geodesic curvature is at least 1. We prove that the normalized relative isoperimetric profile for such a surface is bounded below by that of the Euclidean unit disk, with equality holding at some area fraction in (0,1) if and only if the surface is isometric to the unit disk. The proof uses a differential comparison argument for the isoperimetric profile, based on a suitable non-constant normal variation of isoperimetric curves inspired by the model geometry.

papers.title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
papers.abstract: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.

papers.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. Our policy tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer, which take 13 and 100 hours to identify, against 5 minutes for our mathematically justified 6,924-parameter model.

papers.title: Geometric Rigidity of Manifolds Admitting $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields
papers.abstract: We establish certain integral inequalities for $m$-modified conformal vector fields on compact Riemannian manifolds and derive corresponding triviality and rigidity results. We further obtain integrability conditions for such vector fields and establish an extended Bourguignon-Ezin identity. We then prove that a compact Riemannian manifold admitting a non-trivial closed $m$-modified conformal vector field is isometric to a round sphere under either a constant scalar curvature and positive Ricci curvature assumption or a suitable bound on the Ricci curvature involving the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplace operator. As a consequence, we obtain an extension of a classical sphere characterization result of Yano and Nagano to the corresponding result for a non trivial $m$-modified conformal vector field assumed closed. Finally, we consider a complete Kähler manifold admitting a closed $m$-modified conformal vector field $V$, and show that $V$ is $m$-modified Killing and around a non-zero point of $V$ the manifold splits as the product of the complex Euclidean plane $\mathbb{C}$ and a complete Kähler manifold.

papers.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
papers.abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
papers.abstract: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms
papers.abstract: Let $Φ:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $Θ^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $Φ$. We prove that $Θ^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove derived invariance of all Hodge numbers when $K_X$ is trivial and the conjugate of a holomorphic volume form belongs to the subalgebra of $H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$ generated in degrees one and two. In even dimension, the evaluation isomorphism allows us to compare the ranks of cup product by powers of symplectic two-forms on the Hochschild diagonals. These ranks determine the Hodge numbers individually.

papers.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability
papers.abstract: Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.

papers.title: Double exponential growth for the Euler equation on the whole plane
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible Euler equation on the whole plane $\R^2$, without boundary and without forcing, and we construct two smooth solutions whose vorticity gradient grows fast for all large times. The first solution has finite energy, integrable vorticity and initial data in every Sobolev space. Given any function $Γ(t)$ with $Γ(t)/t\to 0$, the logarithm of its vorticity gradient is not bounded by any multiple of $Γ(t)$, and, at every sufficiently large time $t$, it is larger than any multiple of $t/\log_*t$, where $\log_*$ is the iterated logarithm. The second solution has bounded vorticity, bounded vorticity derivatives on every finite time interval, and a velocity given by the absolutely convergent Biot--Savart integral which grows at most logarithmically in space. Its vorticity gradient grows double exponentially in time for all large times. Its initial vorticity is neither integrable nor square integrable, and its initial velocity and strain are unbounded. Both constructions place infinitely many localized amplification mechanisms far apart from each other in one initial datum. The first one is based on the hyperbolic stagnation point behind a smooth traveling dipole, controlled for long times by an energy--Casimir argument. The second one is based on the hyperbolic point of the Bahouri--Chemin cross on the torus, transported to the plane by spatial dilations and by the uniqueness theory of Serfati solutions.

papers.title: Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Arambašić et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.

papers.title: Random Configurations and Fourier Decoupling
papers.abstract: We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.

papers.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
papers.abstract: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.

papers.title: Resolvent Ellipsoid for Minty Set Inclusions
papers.abstract: We study Minty set inclusion on a compact convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with a set-valued operator $A : \mathcal{X} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}^d$. Under the Minty promise, the goal is to compute $x \in \mathcal{X}$ and $u \in A(x)$ such that $\sup_{y \in \mathcal{X}} \langle u, x - y \rangle \le \varepsilon$. Our approach is geometric and we work in the fixed-scale constrained-resolvent oracle model, where a query at anchor $a$ is assumed to return a resolvent point $x^+$ together with the Yosida vector $g_η(a) = (a - x^+)/η$. We prove that each oracle response yields a sharp dichotomy: either the returned point provides an $\varepsilon$-SVI certificate, or the Yosida vector defines a strict separating normal for the Minty set. Thus, a single black-box resolvent query supplies either a certified candidate solution or a valid geometric cut. Combining this separation principle with the ellipsoid method, we obtain RESOLVENT-ELLIPSOID, an algorithm that computes an $\varepsilon$-SVI in $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box oracle calls to the fixed-scale constrained resolvent. For monotone inclusions, our algorithm gives, to our knowledge, the first $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\mathrm{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box guarantee in the fixed-scale resolvent model.

papers.title: Rational knots, quivers, and tails of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials
papers.abstract: We use the knots-quivers correspondence to prove that the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial of a rational knot has a tail and give an explicit formula for calculating the tail in terms of the quiver.

papers.title: Transformations of Hilbert Module Reference Frames
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a functorial characterization of Hilbert module classical and quantum reference frames. Using the functorial characterization, we construct a category for equivariant couplings and Hilbert module reference frames. We prove the construction of the reference frame system from the equivariant coupling data yields a functor. We also deduce a ``unitary" groupoid as frame transformations for Hilbert module reference frames of a fixed Hilbert module dynamical system. We provide some examples of these frame transformations in the case of the indistinguishable classical two state switch and in the case of Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
papers.abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

papers.title: Pointed Hopf Algebras from Pale Braidings in Characteristic 2
papers.abstract: We determine Nichols algebras associated with several families of pale braidings over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. For the rank-$4$ families under consideration, we obtain presentations by generators and relations, explicit monomial bases and dimension formulas. We also study families of arbitrary rank consisting of a two-dimensional pale block and several points, including cases with both vanishing and nonvanishing interaction parameters. Realizations as Yetter--Drinfeld modules over suitable finite abelian groups yield finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebras by bosonization.

papers.title: Universal and Reciprocating Domains in Classes of Continua and Beyond
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the notions of reciprocating domains in classes of topological spaces. A reciprocating domain is a member of a class that maps onto every member which maps onto it. We provide general characterizations, showing in particular that in upward directed classes reciprocating domains coincide with universal domains. We investigate these domains in several classes of compact metrizable spaces and continua. We also construct a chainable universal domain admitting a continuous monotone surjection onto a pseudoarc although every nondegenerate subcontinuum of the domain contains an arc. In particular, a chainable reciprocating domain need not contain a pseudoarc.

papers.title: Optimal adaptive finite element methods in $W^{1,p}$
papers.abstract: We prove linear convergence and algebraic rate optimality of an adaptive finite element method for the Dirichlet Poisson problem in W1p. We assume well-posedness of the continuous problem and discrete inf-sup stability over the refinement family. We verify both hypotheses when p is sufficiently close to 2, without requiring convexity of the domain. The Galerkin equations remain unchanged, while the residual estimator and Dörfler marking use the target exponent p. Linear convergence holds for every fixed marking fraction between zero and one. For sufficiently small marking fractions and marked sets of nearly minimal cardinality, the method attains the best algebraic rates for W1p approximation together with data oscillation. The main ingredient is a Banach-space extension of Feischl's relaxed quasi-orthogonality, proved under discrete inf-sup stability.

papers.title: Nonasymptotic causal structure learning in generalized linear DAGs with continuous optimization
papers.abstract: We study the problem of learning directed acyclic graphs from observational data in nonlinear models and provide finite-sample, nonasymptotic statistical guarantees in these models. Although widely studied, statistical guarantees for gradient-based methods in nonlinear models are missing from the literature. Under a generalized linear model for each node, we analyze a global nonsmooth objective combining an exact acyclicity constraint with a quasi-minimax concave penalty, which can be optimized via standard gradient-based solvers. We establish finite-sample guarantees under this model, including the most widely used logistic and Poisson models. Experiments corroborate structure recovery accuracy and computational performance, including both standardized data and negative controls as baselines.

papers.title: Collapsing flat manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
papers.abstract: We study volume collapse of compact connected flat manifolds with nonempty totally geodesic boundary and uniformly bounded diameter. We prove subsequential Gromov--Hausdorff convergence to compact flat orbifolds, allowing reflector loci, and describe the limit using the canonical involutions of the doubles. We distinguish the cases in which the maximal distance to the boundary tends to zero or to a positive limit, and classify all possible limits in dimension three.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface. The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.

papers.title: On sinks and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
papers.abstract: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fréchet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.

papers.title: Pauli propagation in adaptive local frames
papers.abstract: The cost of Pauli propagation depends on the local basis in which the evolving operator is expanded. We show that its Pauli complexity splits into an occupation part, invariant under local rotations and bounded from below by the operator mass and length distributions, and a flavour part that a suitable basis can remove. We introduce frame-adaptive Pauli propagation (FAPP), which rotates the basis of every qubit, gate by gate, to the principal axes of the operator's local polarisation, exactly and within the memory structure of Pauli propagation. This simple rule achieves most of what the best local frame can, and the polarisation predicts how much any local frame can gain. In the Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields, FAPP lowers the truncation error at fixed memory by up to an order of magnitude and the memory by a size-independent factor of three; on the infinite two-dimensional lattice it needs up to seven times fewer strings for a given certified accuracy, and in Clifford circuits doped with T gates two to eight times fewer.

papers.title: A software infrastructure proposal for mathematical research with AI agents
papers.abstract: In 2026, AI agents began to produce mathematical results. They formalize complete theorems and settle open problems faster than a research group can review the results. The difficulty is shifting to organizing that output, deciding which results to trust and understanding them as a group. Current tools address particular problems or assist individual researchers, and none of them is designed as the shared working environment of a research group. We propose the design of a self-hosted environment in which a group of people and agents does its daily mathematical work. It consists of a small open core, which each group deploys with the resources it has and adapts through extensions. The core records who did what and gives every message and result a stable address. We also outline how the formal libraries of different groups, maintained mostly by agents, can form a network. We describe Stemma, an early prototype that implements part of the proposal, and illustrate it with a synthetic example.

papers.title: Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
papers.abstract: We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $π$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(πz))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(πz))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $μ_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $μ_f(O_{1,2}) = μ_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $Φ_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}Φ_j(z)$ with Koenigs Taylor jets $c_2(1) = -\frac{13}{2}π^2$ and $d_2(2) = -\frac{9}{2}π^2$; (3) the Schwarzian derivative is strictly negative on $\mathbb{Z}$ ($S(f)(n) \le 3π^2 - \frac{3}{8}π^4 \approx -6.9196 < 0$), and a repelling Julia 2-cycle $O_{\mathrm{rep}} \subset J(f)$ ($μ\approx 1.2148 > 1$) isolates $B(O_{1,2})$; (4) on $(\mathbb{Z}_2, μ_{\mathrm{Haar}})$, the 2-adic Lyapunov exponent $λ_{\mathrm{Haar}} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(3/4) \approx -0.143841 < 0$ equals $\frac{1}{2}\ln|μ_f(O_{1,2})|$; and (5) we certify 20 theorems in Lean 4 (anc/CollatzAttractor.lean, 0 sorry). These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.

papers.title: Stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam equation with distributed damping and interior time delay
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.

papers.title: Polar foliations on the Cayley plane
papers.abstract: We classify polar foliations on the Cayley projective plane, completing the classification of polar foliations on compact rank one symmetric spaces.

papers.title: Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.

papers.title: The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
papers.abstract: We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.

papers.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
papers.abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

papers.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
papers.abstract: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.

papers.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

papers.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract: We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences. For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class. The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.

papers.title: Proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture: An Exposition
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of a recent proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, which states that every degree-$d$ polynomial $p : \{0,1\}^n \to [0,1]$ has a variable of influence at least $\mathrm{poly}(\mathrm{Var}(p)/d)$. This implies that quantum query algorithms for decision problems can be efficiently simulated classically on most inputs. It also yields a near-equivalence between the status of the $\mathsf{BPP}$ vs. $\mathsf{BQP}$ problem in the random oracle and unrelativized worlds. We organize the proof around four main steps and discuss how each connects to the literature on the analysis of boolean functions and probabilistic combinatorics. To bring out the key ideas, we do not optimize parameters, and our presentation yields weaker exponents than the original. $\textbf{Authors' note.}$ The proof was discovered by David Turturean using a research system developed at Physical Superintelligence (PSI), in combination with a non-public Anthropic model. The proof was then shared with the authors, who worked to understand it and prepare this exposition. Anthropic's public models were used in this process. The authors did not receive financial compensation from Anthropic or PSI. This article is not intended for publication at a conference or in a journal.

papers.title: Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares
papers.abstract: This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.

papers.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.

papers.title: When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals
papers.abstract: We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order.
