Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

papers.title: Coherent Conversion of an Interacting Dark-State-Polariton Condensate into a Photonic Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.abstract: An interacting condensate can retain an observable imprint of its preparation after the interactions are switched off. For light, accessing this regime requires separating the formation of a photon condensate from the material medium that redistributes its energy. We investigate a multimode-cavity scheme in which an interacting dark-state-polariton condensate is coherently converted into a confined photonic Bose-Einstein condensate as the atom-cavity coupling is removed. The polariton mass, matter fraction, and particle number control the condensate occupation during preparation. Remarkably, changing the mass also modifies the condensate's response to repulsion through the spatial overlap of its orbitals, even when the entire single-particle spectrum is held fixed. Ideal mode-preserving conversion conserves the full natural-orbital occupation spectrum, while finite-time few-body calculations show that additional occupation changes during transfer are much smaller than those established during interacting preparation. Once decoupled from matter, the photons evolve under the free cavity Hamiltonian while retaining correlations acquired in the interacting gas. Interference between cavity modes produces oscillations in the photon density, while resonant pair correlations persist after interaction removal and distinguish the resulting photon state from a quadratic thermal state with the same one-body density matrix.

papers.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
papers.abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Ampère equations with Hölder continuous right-hand sides
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Ampère equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<α<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^α$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,β}$ bounds for every fixed $0<β<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.

papers.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
papers.abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.

papers.title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
papers.abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
papers.abstract: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.

papers.title: An Arbitrary-Order Distributional Finite Element Method for the Curl--Dev Grad Stokes System
papers.abstract: We develop an arbitrary-order distributional finite element method for the three-dimensional curl--dev grad Stokes system governed by the Hessian complex. On tetrahedral meshes, the method couples degree-$(k+1)$ nonconforming symmetric-tensor virtual elements, degree-$k$ tangential-normal continuous traceless tensor elements, and Raviart--Thomas elements of index $k$, without additional virtual-element stabilization. Building on zero-extension curl--div theory, we derive a well-posed distributional saddle-point formulation with an $H(\operatorname{div})$ vector multiplier. A divergence-augmented discrete norm equivalence controls the full Raviart--Thomas space modulo translations and underpins mesh-uniform stability for each fixed $k\ge0$. We establish optimal $O(h^{k+1})$ energy error estimates and an optimal $O(h^{k+2})$ $L^2$ error estimate for the full symmetric-tensor approximation, under suitable regularity and load approximation assumptions. As an application, the method supplies the Stokes block of a decoupled triharmonic scheme with optimal Hessian error estimates. Numerical experiments support the predicted convergence rates for computable quantities.

papers.title: Adaptive Quantum Metrology of Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: We develop a feedback-controlled quantum metrology scheme to probe weak gravitational waves (GWs) through their direct energy exchange with light. Adaptive SU(2) direction control, based on current estimates of the GW frequency and phase, allows the frequency shifts acquired in successive interaction intervals to add rather than cancel. The resulting persistent frequency difference is converted into an optical phase difference for interferometric readout. We further extend the scheme to elliptically polarized GWs using two transverse sensing channels separated by $45^\circ$ to probe the $+$ and $\times$ components independently. After the GW interaction, the two signals are mapped onto orthogonal polarization modes, enabling phase accumulation along a common path. We derive the corresponding quantum Fisher information matrix and find a $T_{\rm int}^2T_{\rm ph}^2$ scaling in the ideal coherent regime. For a fixed-photon-number probe, the sensitivity shows Heisenberg-like $1/n$ scaling in the ideal case.

papers.title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Data centers can provide power flexibility through the scheduling of computing workloads, cooling systems, and batteries. Characterizing this flexibility online is useful but challenging because of the complex coupling among these resources. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a role-conditioned cross-head DeepSets reinforcement learning approach to characterize the power flexibility interval of a data center at each time step. First, we formulate the flexibility characterization problem as a Markov decision process that jointly models the three resources under a carbon budget, with actions specifying the upper and lower endpoints of the power flexibility interval. We then design DeepSets actor and critic that represent delay-tolerant workloads as an unordered set, enabling the proposed approach to accommodate varying numbers of workloads with a fixed number of trainable parameters. Finally, because maximizing the width of the flexibility interval requires moving its endpoints in opposite directions, we develop a role-conditioned cross-head decoder that distinguishes their respective roles while keeping them coordinated. Case studies on the Google Cluster Data show that the proposed approach provides more than twice the daily flexibility of the standard soft actor-critic method with nearly zero carbon overshoot while using 87.7% fewer trainable parameters.

papers.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_α C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(α)$ and letting $C_α=\langleα\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_α$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $α$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[α]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_θH$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
papers.abstract: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $β_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.

papers.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schrödinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

papers.title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2πsx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.

papers.title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
papers.abstract: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.

papers.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
papers.abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

papers.title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
papers.abstract: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

papers.title: On-the-Fly Reduced Bases Through the Lens of Augmented Krylov Methods
papers.abstract: On-the-fly reduced order models (ROMs) are widely used in applications where multiple queries of large-scale models are required in an iterative method, like PDE-constrained optimization or fluid-structure interaction. When compared to classical offline--online ROMs, they have the advantage of being agnostic to any precomputed training data, mesh or geometry, which makes them more general linear/nonlinear solver accelerators. The main goal of this work is to study the effect of using a reduced basis constructed on-the-fly to accelerate a restarted Krylov algorithm, and to formally bridge this category of data-driven methods with classical augmented Krylov methods. The guiding principles of on-the-fly reduced basis will be translated into the framework of Krylov subspace methods, for a Petrov-Galerkin projection method. Previous corrections generated by the algorithm are stored in a snapshot matrix, and a singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to determine a reduced subspace containing the most significant directions. It will be shown that this approach can be embedded in the framework of Krylov methods with augmented or deflated restart, but with a different, data-driven recycling strategy. An analytical study will be presented to determine the consequences of augmentation by ROM-based vectors. Numerical experiments on a convection-diffusion problem with various degrees of convection will show that the proposed methodology yields results comparable to classical iterative linear solvers in some regimes, especially for nearly symmetric or skew-symmetric operators. At equal sizes of the augmentation basis, the convergence was sometimes faster with the proposed framework than with deflation methods.

papers.title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
papers.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and let $τ(G)$ be the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. We prove $τ(G)\le2ν(G)$ when each edge belongs to at most four triangles, the edges belonging to four triangles form components with at most two edges, and the maximum average degree is at most $25/2$. No upper bound on maximum vertex degree is imposed. We also localize the density condition. Let $K$ be the Hifumi core, defined as the vertex set of the 4-core of the spanning subgraph formed by edges belonging to at least three triangles. It suffices to impose the density condition on $G[K]$, including all original edges between vertices of $K$. More generally, when the four-triangle edges have maximum degree at most two, reductions produce a subgraph $R\subseteq G[K]$ with $τ(G)-2ν(G)\leτ(R)-2ν(R)$. Consequently an empty core gives a density-free sufficient condition. For the first graph class, a quantitative surplus argument strengthens both the global and localized density conditions to the strict bound $25/2+2/56775$. The proof combines edge reductions, discharging, finite certificates and a weak König--Egerváry lemma for links of arbitrary order. The general conjecture and the removal of the density condition from the first graph class remain unresolved here.

papers.title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
papers.abstract: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial-Query Approximation for Consistent Submodular Maximization with Short Lookahead
papers.abstract: Elements arrive one at a time, and after each arrival an algorithm holds a set of at most $k$ arrived elements. Its goal is a held set whose value under a monotone submodular function is close to the best value that $k$ arrived elements can achieve. The recourse of an update is the number of elements inserted into or removed from the held set, and we require it to be bounded independently of $k$ and of the number $n$ of arrivals. With evaluations only on sets of arrived elements and polynomially many of them, the best ratio a randomized algorithm can achieve is $2-\sqrt{2}\approx0.5858$. We show that seeing future arrivals raises the best ratio for polynomially many evaluations to $1-1/e\approx0.6321$, for deterministic and for randomized algorithms; no algorithm with polynomially many evaluations exceeds $1-1/e$, even when all elements are available at once. For every $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic algorithm that sees the next $\lceil\varepsilon k/3\rceil$ arrivals keeps a set of value at least $1-1/e-\varepsilon$ times the optimum at every time, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ elements per arrival and makes $(n+1)^{O(\varepsilon^{-2})}$ evaluations. With the whole arrival sequence known in advance, a deterministic algorithm attains the same ratio with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ changes per arrival. A randomized algorithm with the same short lookahead makes $O(n^2k)$ evaluations, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ elements per arrival, and attains the same ratio in expectation at each fixed time. The main tool is a greedy algorithm with an explicit guarantee for each of its partial solutions combined with each initial segment of the known future arrivals. A second tool moves between two such solutions one element at a time while keeping the value high, and the deterministic algorithm times each move using upper bounds on the optimum from failed searches.

papers.title: The Escobar Constant for Two-dimensional Disks
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface homeomorphic to a closed disk, with boundary length $L$. We establish sharp upper bounds for its Escobar constant under upper bounds on the Gaussian curvature. If $K_g\leq 0$, then $I(M,g)\leq 2/π$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to a Euclidean disk. If $K_g\leqκ$ for some $κ>0$, $L<2π/\sqrtκ$, and $\operatorname{Area}_g(M)<2π/κ$, then $I(M,g)\leq\frac{4}{\sqrtκL}\arcsin(\frac{\sqrtκL}{2π})$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to the geodesic disk of the same perimeter contained in an open hemisphere of the sphere of constant curvature $κ$. We also discuss the higher order Escobar constant for planar domains. In particular, we construct counterexamples to Hassannezhad and Siffert's conjecture.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
papers.abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

papers.title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
papers.abstract: Bar-Lev and Letac (2025) introduced the concept of chainability of infinitely divisible distributions on $\mathbb R$. In this note, we show that a simpler notion of chainability can be used for infinitely divisible distributions on $[0,\infty)$. We derive some properties and give a probabilistic interpretation in terms of so-called size-biased distributions. As an application, we discuss simulation from size-biased distributions associated with an important class of tempered stable distributions.

papers.title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations in a bounded domain in two and three space dimensions. We establish the local exact controllability around a constant equilibrium state. Our proof relies on the observability and controllability analysis of a suitably reformulated linearized system, together with a fixed point argument in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main novelty of this paper is to overcome the structural difficulties arising from the divergence free constraint and the strong coupling between the fluid and magnetic variables. To accommodate the solenoidal constraint, we introduce a magnetic potential formulation and develop a mixed coordinate approach.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hatβ$ we realize $π_1(S^3\setminus\hatβ)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM
papers.abstract: Sparse hierarchical nonlinear programming (SH-NLP) based on the $\ell_0$-norm provides a powerful framework for integrated, efficient hierarchical decision-making in robot kinematic control, for example in the presence of a large set of possible end-effector candidate locations. While Sequential Sparse Hierarchical Quadratic Programming (S-SHQP) with interior-point method based SHQP sub-problem solvers exploit the hierarchical, sparse structure of such problems, they are less amenable to effective warm-starting between subsequent, coherent control steps. In this work, we formulate an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to efficiently solve related SHQP sub-problems. We introduce efficient substitutions for auxiliary variables representing $\ell_0$-norm surrogates. The solver efficiently handles separable decision functions by evaluating linear algebra expressions in the appropriate order. Results in large-scale kinematic and dynamic control show reduced computation times of up to 23.5% compared with a structure-exploiting interior-point method in low- to moderate-accuracy regimes. Furthermore, hierarchical decision-making is extended to whole-body dynamic control for humanoid walking, where the need for high-accuracy solutions is highlighted.

papers.title: Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
papers.abstract: We propose a sampling-based dual model predictive control (MPC) approach that combines belief propagation with parameterized feedback policy optimization. By sampling uncertain dynamics and process noise, we approximate the evolution of the hyperstate over the prediction horizon, allowing future control decisions to adapt to anticipated observations and belief updates. This enables the controller to account for the future value of information without explicit exploration incentives. We establish almost-sure uniform convergence of the sample-average objective to the finite-horizon expected objective over a compact policy class. The approach is specialized to Bayesian linear regression and evaluated on stochastic systems with constant and time-varying uncertain dynamics. We compare our approach to certainty equivalent control, and an MPC that optimizes over open-loop control sequences rather than feedback policies, demonstrating the benefits of our method in terms of both control performance and information gain.

papers.title: A reachability criterion for spectrally factorable SPDC in coupled waveguides without periodic poling
papers.abstract: Producing spectrally pure photon pairs by spontaneous parametric down-conversion without periodic poling would broaden the choice of nonlinear materials. It requires optical modes that provide both phase matching and suitable group velocities. We derive a joint reachability criterion for a constant-cross-section coupler with a nonlinear main guide and a linear auxiliary. In a two-mode description, phase closure fixes the hybridization parameter that also determines the main-guide participation and the attainable group-delay ratio. This relation screens material and mode pairs and specifies detuning and participation targets for full-vector refinement. A first-order purity map connects the reachable delay ratio and bandwidth--length product to the photon-pair spectrum. A full-vector AlN/TiO$_2$ feasibility example satisfies direct phase matching with a ratio of pump--idler to pump--signal group-delay mismatches of $-0.899$ and yields a calculated unfiltered Schmidt purity of 0.789 over 5 mm. The criterion links phase closure, dispersion control, and nonlinear participation when assessing coupled-waveguide sources beyond periodically poled materials.

papers.title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
papers.abstract: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) requires the calculation of highly accurate electronic-structure energies and nuclear forces at every time step, which can quickly become computationally expensive. Sample-based quantum diagonalization offers a route to such calculations on quantum hardware, but its use in AIMD simulations has so far been limited to active spaces of about 20 qubits. In these spaces, exact diagonalization is tractable, and the quantum circuits are typically built from standard coupled-cluster amplitudes. Here, we introduce SqDRIFT-AIMD, which combines randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT) with analytical nuclear gradients. With SqDRIFT-AIMD, we obtain more accurate ground-state energies than the conventional coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) driven AIMD simulation for the $40$-qubit active space. We apply SqDRIFT-AIMD to study the dynamics of proton transfer in the Zundel cation, using circuits executed on IBM Heron r3 quantum processors. SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the $40$-qubit double-well PES and stay within a few m$E_\text{h}$ of CCSD at 52 qubits. The $40$-qubit SqDRIFT-AIMD trajectory tracks the SHCI-driven proton transfer to within $1.33$ mÅ and exhibits excellent total energy conservation, with a standard deviation of only $0.245$ m$E_\text{h}$. These results extend quantum-centric AIMD to active spaces beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

papers.title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
papers.abstract: We determine the interval between the varieties generated by the nonempty and full power semirings of a semigroup satisfying \(xy\approx x^2\). It has two elements for a one-element semigroup, three for a nontrivial left-zero or null semigroup, and seven otherwise, without any finiteness assumption. In the seven-element case the interval is \([\Rvar,\Rvar^0]\), where \(\Rvar=\Mod_{\rm ai}\{xy\approx xz\}\) and \(\Rvar^0\) is its zero-adjunction variety. Every word absorption valid in \(\Rvar\) but not in \(\Rvar^0\) is equivalent over \(\Rvar^0\) to one of six relative identities. We give exact absorption criteria and finite bases for all seven varieties. Three have basis rank two and four have basis rank three; their two-generated free algebras have orders \(15\), \(24\), or \(35\). We also count the finite-rank free algebras of both endpoints.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a line-search quasi-Newton (LSQN) method for discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs). The method maintains an inverse model to approximate the inverse of the current policy Jacobian and refines it through an inner learning procedure that preserves existing secant conditions and achieves the prescribed accuracy in at most $n$ queries in exact arithmetic for an MDP with $n$ states, even when the initial inverse model is singular. A sign-based direction correction combined with an Armijo line search ensures monotonic decrease of the Bellman residual norm across policy changes without requiring a value-iteration fallback. We prove global Q-linear residual convergence and local Q-superlinear convergence of the value iterates from arbitrary finite initial value vectors and inverse models, without requiring a unique optimal policy. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against nine baselines, while public benchmarks demonstrate that the inner learning procedure typically requires far fewer than $n$ learning queries.

papers.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
papers.abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

papers.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
papers.abstract: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.

papers.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
papers.abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

papers.title: Non-log-concave $τ$-polynomials of regular graphs
papers.abstract: For any simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for any $j\ge 1$ and $x^{\langle0\rangle}=1$. Brenti (1992) introduced the $τ$-polynomial and its augmented version, defined by $$τ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}c_jx^j, \qquad \overlineτ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}j!c_jx^j.$$ He asked whether $τ(G,x)$ always has only real roots and whether $\overlineτ(G,x)$ always has a log-concave coefficient sequence. In this paper, we show that for any integer $d\ge 4$, there exists an integer $h_d$ such that, for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$, the coefficient sequence of $τ(G,x)$ fails to be log-concave. This failure also occurs for $\overlineτ(G,x)$, and Newton's inequalities imply that $τ(G,x)$ has nonreal roots. Thus both questions have counterexamples among regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.

papers.title: Bridging Gaps with Tensor Networks: From the Haldane Gap and Beyond
papers.abstract: Proofs generated by large language models are often difficult to understand, generalize, or formalize directly. Here we verify, digest, and formalize OpenAI's computer-assisted proof of a uniform gap in the periodic spin-1 Heisenberg chain using tensor-network diagrams and Lean 4. Reading the partition-function network along space and imaginary time shows how finite-ring bounds propagate across doubled lengths and inverse temperatures to all longer even rings, sharpening the spin-1 bound from the same finite inputs by a factor of 19 to $Δ_L > 0.0729$ for all even $L \geq 36$. We identify reflection positivity as the general condition behind the proof and certify uniform gaps in seven additional spin chains and ladders. More broadly, digesting machine-generated proofs into transparent physical mechanisms yields sharper bounds, broader theorems, and reusable formal verifications.

papers.title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
papers.abstract: We study the Zakharov system on an arbitrary fixed rectangular two-dimensional torus with initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$. For the Schrödinger regularity $s$, Kishimoto proved local well-posedness for $1/2\leq s\leq1$ and global well-posedness for $9/14<s<1$ below the Euclidean cubic ground-state mass. Under the same mass condition, we prove global well-posedness for every $1/2<s<1$, with polynomial bounds for the Sobolev norms. We add quartic and quintic corrections to Kishimoto's resonantly modified energy. The main difficulty is to cancel the interactions obstructing the global iteration without introducing singular coefficients near resonance or losing control of the higher-order terms generated by differentiation. The coefficients exploit cancellations between successive nonlinear interactions. Away from resonance, they cancel the problematic terms; near resonance, algebraic rearrangements avoid division by small phases and preserve sufficient frequency decay. For every $s<1/2$, we also construct solutions with arbitrarily small initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$ whose wave component blows up in finite time while the Schrödinger component remains bounded in $H^s$. We combine explicit approximate solutions supported on three Fourier modes with stability at $H^{1/2}\times L^2$. Choosing successively larger frequencies controls the nonlinear interactions among infinitely many approximate solutions and makes the accumulated errors summable, while their wave amplitudes produce blow-up. These results identify $s=1/2$ as the threshold between global well-posedness and the existence of such blow-up solutions, with the endpoint unresolved.

papers.title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
papers.abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

papers.title: Exact sampling beyond Fock inputs and linear optics: photon-number superpositions, photonic matrix-product states, adaptive and non-linear circuits
papers.abstract: Clifford and Clifford's algorithm samples single-photon boson sampling exactly, one output mode at a time, by adding the input photons in a uniformly random order. We extend this construction to other input states and to adaptive and non-linear circuits. It applies whenever non-negative weights on output prefixes and input sets satisfy one marginal identity, a set-chain lemma: the random-order sampler is then exact at one weight evaluation per candidate mode, and it gives the posterior over the hidden input set. We build four exact samplers on it. For sources in a superposition of vacuum and one photon, the weights are rectangular permanents on an offset input set, and the cost has the exponent of single photons under loss. For photonic matrix-product states of bond dimension $χ$, a gap-by-gap Kraus contraction turns each weight into a short sum of squared amplitudes. For adaptive linear optics, the chain starts from the posterior given the adaptive counts and rejects chains that contradict them. For a single-mode non-linear phase the identity fails, and rejection from linear branches is exact with acceptance $1/\|c\|_1^2$. All four samplers agree with strong simulation on small instances, and cost models put adaptive sampling with up to three adaptive modes within $10\%$ of single photons and a non-linear site at $\varphi=π/2$ at about $4\times$.

papers.title: Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields associated with semisprays on Lie algebroids. First, we characterize compatible transverse variations in terms of Lie algebroid morphisms. This characterization leads to a variational description of Jacobi sections: a section along an integral curve of a semispray is a Jacobi section if and only if it arises as the infinitesimal variation of a compatible transverse variation of a dynamical variation satisfying a suitable condition on its image in the base. We also investigate the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields through the anchor map. We prove that every Jacobi section projects to a Jacobi field, and establish a converse when the corresponding base variation is contained in a single leaf of the characteristic foliation.

papers.title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
papers.abstract: We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is governed by the ergodic invasion exponent, which decides the predator's fate pathwise. When the predator becomes extinct, the closure of the union of the fibres of the pullback attractor equals the minimal uniform attracting set if and only if the upper worst-case exponent is nonpositive, and otherwise the inclusion is strict and the latter is invariant under no realisation. When the predator persists, the essential closure of the union of the fibres contains, for every frozen environment in which the predator invades, the equilibrium or a periodic orbit of the frozen system, and every state the control system can reach from them. The predator is uniformly persistent when the lower worst-case exponent is positive and almost surely not when it is negative. The ergodic exponent lies below its deterministic counterpart by an amount comparable to the curvature of the response times the variance of the accessible fraction.

papers.title: Weak $λ$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mrówka spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $λ$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $λ$-space is a $λ$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $ω_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $λ$-set is a $λ$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>ω_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.

papers.title: A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{β(N-1)}$, $0\leβ<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $β$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $β=0$ and, for $β>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ is attained for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $β>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $β\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.

papers.title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
papers.abstract: We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.

papers.title: The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
papers.abstract: The Herzog--Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.

papers.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
papers.abstract: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $Σ(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $Σ(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $Σ(p_c)$ completely: $Σ(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.

papers.title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
papers.abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.

papers.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
papers.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilization, and more selective excitation. Our results combine MOVPE growth, deterministic device integration, and telecom C-band emission, providing a route toward scalable semiconductor quantum light sources for fiber-based quantum networks.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk
papers.abstract: We give a complete characterization of the holomorphic isometric embeddings $F:(\mathbb{D},k\,ds^2)\rightarrow (\mathbb{G}_2,ds^2)$ of the unit disk into the symmetrized bidisk with respect to the Bergman metric up to a scalar constant. We show that the isometric constant $k$ can take only the values $k=1$ and $k=3$. For $k=3$, we prove that $(2z,z^2)$ is the unique isometry up to a reparametrization. For $k=1$, we construct an isometric embedding which intersects the royal variety at a single point and does not admit a holomorphic lift to the bidisk via the symmetrization map. We further show that this isometric embedding is unique up to reparametrizations. Finally, none of the isometries are totally geodesic.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.abstract: The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Taylor Formulas for H-structures
papers.abstract: We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $ξ$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamondξ$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.

papers.title: DMP-Oriented Anisotropic Mesh Adaptation for SUPG Finite Element Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Diffusion Problems
papers.abstract: We study discrete bound preservation for fully discrete piecewise-linear streamline upwind Petrov--Galerkin (SUPG) finite element approximations of time-dependent convection--diffusion equations on anisotropic triangular meshes. Although the continuous homogeneous-source problem satisfies a parabolic maximum principle, SUPG approximations can exhibit nonphysical undershoots and overshoots. We derive sufficient nodal discrete maximum principle (DMP) conditions that account for the stabilized mass matrix, the combined effects of physical and streamline diffusion, time-step restrictions, and transfer between successive meshes. The analysis identifies a SUPG-effective diffusion tensor and motivates an anisotropic metric aligned with its inverse. We construct a combined metric that retains the effective-tensor geometry while introducing solution-dependent mesh density through recovered Hessian information. The resulting DMP conditions provide a theoretical basis for anisotropic mesh design. Numerical experiments for time-dependent transport problems with isotropic and moderately anisotropic diffusion demonstrate that, under mass-compatible limited SUPG stabilization, the combined metric substantially reduces measured undershoots relative to other methods at matched nominal mesh budgets, although improved bound behavior can carry an accuracy penalty. A controlled tensor--density comparison in the anisotropic transport test supports a contribution from the effective tensor beyond the prescribed mesh density.

papers.title: Improving Analytic Constants via Interpretable AI-Guided Lean Proof Refinement
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. Our key insight is that existing proofs often contain slack in intermediate lemmas, which can be tightened without reconstructing the entire argument. To exploit this structure, we represent proofs as partially-formalized Lean blueprints: human-interpretable dependency graphs of definitions, lemmas, and theorems. An AI agent then iteratively refines the Lean code while preserving the blueprint's dependency structure, allowing local improvements to automatically propagate to a verified final bound. This interpretable structure allows humans to inspect the agent's refinements and understand how local improvements propagate to the final theorem. For Grothendieck's constant ($\mathcal{K}_G$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_G \leq \fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})} - 10^{-17}, $$ an explicit numerical improvement over Krivine's 1977 bound. For Korenblum's constant ($\mathcal{K}_K$), we obtain $$ \mathcal{K}_K \geq 0.356565, $$ improving Wang's 2025 bound of $0.3554$. Our experiments demonstrate the potential of both partial formalization and iterative agentic refinement for interpretable mathematical discovery.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
papers.abstract: Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.

papers.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
papers.abstract: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

papers.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

papers.title: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.

papers.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
papers.abstract: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

papers.title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
papers.abstract: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.

papers.title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.

papers.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
papers.abstract: We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane. It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.

papers.title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
papers.abstract: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.

papers.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

papers.title: An Optimal First-Order Active-Hull Method for Convex Composite Hölder Smooth Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider the problem (P): ${\min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^n}\, f(x)+g(x)$ under the Euclidean geometry, where $f$ is convex and $(M,ν)$-Hölder smooth on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $g$ is proper, closed and convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a generalized linear minimization oracle (GLMO), and has bounded domain with diameter $D$. An first-order active-hull (AH) method has access to both the first-order oracle (FO) of $f$ and the GLMO of $g$, and outputs a point that lies in the convex hull of all the past GLMO returns. We propose a new first-order AH method for solving (P), which is based on our newly developed ``recentered homotopy smoothing framework''. We show that in the high-dimensional regime, this method achieves the optimal FO and GLMO complexties simultaneously for all $ν\in[0,1]$.

papers.title: Bias-free superconducting microwave nonreciprocity from a passive nonlinear resonator
papers.abstract: Routing microwave tones in a nonreciprocal fashion in a superconducting chip usually requires an external bias, commonly in the form of static magnetic fields, pump tones or temporal modulation. Here we demonstrate microwave nonreciprocity in a bias-free, passive platform, a single nonlinear superconducting resonator patterned in one film without Josephson junctions.
