Our conditional oracle separation provides evidence that such structured quantum hardness can nevertheless arise from unstructured sources. Complementing this result, we rule out fully black-box quantum reductions of worst-case quantum hardness in $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ to post-quantum injective one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation. This barrier excludes a broad class of black-box approaches to deriving structured quantum hardness from generic cryptographic primitives, providing partial evidence that the non-black-box techniques in our first result are essential.

papers.title: The interface scattering law for run-and-tumble kinetic models
papers.abstract: For microorganisms with run-and-tumble motility, kinetic models provide a well-established description of transport in smoothly varying environments. Sharp signal changes, however, can induce asymmetric interface responses. A motivating example is the response to dark-light boundaries: cells moving into the light largely maintain their direction, whereas those entering the dark are effectively scattered back. Through an interface-layer analysis of pathway-based kinetic equations, we formally derive effective interface conditions for the limiting run-and-tumble model. These velocity-nonlocal conditions capture non-adiabatic scattering near signal discontinuities, linking intracellular sensory dynamics to transport across sharp environmental boundaries. For a two-velocity model, they reduce to an explicit transmission matrix. We assess the interface law numerically using biologically motivated parameters for E. coli chemotaxis.

papers.title: The Higman-Sims graph and a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$
papers.abstract: The Higman-Sims graph is the unique strongly regular graph with parameters $(100,22,0,6)$. In this paper, we show that the only distance-regular antipodal double cover of the Higman-Sims graph is its bipartite double cover. Our main tool is a geometric construction of the Steiner system $S(3,6,22)$.

papers.title: Random Reshuffling for Smooth Convex Optimization: Dominates Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is one of the most classical optimization algorithms with favorable theoretical guarantees, yet its practical implementation differs subtly from its well-known form and is often referred to as Shuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent (Shuffling SGD). A particularly popular strategy in Shuffling SGD is Random Reshuffling (RR), which has achieved great empirical success. Despite its strong performance, RR has long been considered a heuristic due to a lack of theoretical support. Over the last decade, people have finally established provable convergence rates for RR, thus justifying its observed superiority. However, for smooth convex optimization, two clouds over the convergence theory of RR remain. According to current theory, Shuffling SGD under RR converges only when the stepsize is smaller than a threshold proportional to $1/n$, where $n$ is the number of summands in the objective (or the number of data points). Consequently, the optimally tuned theoretical rate of Shuffling SGD under RR is strictly worse than that of SGD when the number of epochs is smaller than another threshold proportional to $n$. These two restrictions heavily limit the applicability of existing theories and leave a critical mismatch with practice. In this work, for the first time, we prove that RR dominates SGD in smooth convex optimization for any reasonable stepsize after any finite number of epochs, thereby addressing a longstanding open question. Moreover, we establish new algorithm-dependent lower bounds for RR and SGD, respectively. Altogether, these results yield (nearly) sharp worst-case characterizations of RR and SGD. Furthermore, we develop a shuffling-based method to optimize functions satisfying the quadratic growth condition, a strict relaxation of strong convexity, and derive a new complexity bound improving existing results proved under stronger assumptions.

papers.title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
papers.abstract: Weak value (WV) describes the amplified response of a meter when the measured system undergoes postselection. While conventional WV theory mainly rests on a single system-meter interaction setting, it remains unexplored whether WV can act as an effective pointer for sequential quantum measurements under postselection. Here we introduce the concept of WVs to the setting of sequential quantum measurements and quantum trajectories. We find that WV naturally emerges in postselected quantum trajectories of sequential weak measurements, by establishing a connection between the WV of the measured observable and the postselected statistics of quantum trajectories. Using sequential weak measurements on a qubit or an oscillator implemented by Ramsey interferometry with an ancilla qubit, we show that postselection shifts the collective record polarization away from the unconditioned ones, with an effective bias described by the WV. Our predictions are feasible to test in various platforms.

papers.title: Holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi operator on Kähler C-spaces
papers.abstract: We study holomorphic sectional curvature and the Calabi curvature operator on compact Kähler manifolds. First we show that every homogeneous Kähler metric on a generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For the standard homogeneous Kähler-Einstein metric with Einstein constant 2, it is shown that the spectrum of the Calabi operator lies in $(-2,2]$. We determine its sharp upper bound in terms of the anticanonical degrees and characterize the 2-eigenspace. The spectral bounds imply nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature, proving conjectures of Ni and Zheng. We also show that these conditions do not characterize homogeneity: we construct a nonhomogeneous Kähler-Einstein 13-fold whose Calabi spectrum lies strictly inside $(-2,2)$ after the same normalization, as well as nonhomogeneous examples in dimensions 4 and 5. The proofs involve an integral identity for holomorphic sectional curvature, projective embeddings, root-space estimates, and explicit metrics on projective bundles.

papers.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
papers.abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.

papers.title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
papers.abstract: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

papers.title: Discrete history operators: Exact state-space realization for sequence memory
papers.abstract: A prescribed finite-dimensional analysis of an evolving discrete history need not admit an exact recurrence driven only by its current state and the entering input. We study exact realizations of causal linear discrete history operators (DHOs). Operator factorization and kernel inclusion characterize exact closure, while the cross-projection defect characterizes closure failure for orthonormal analyses. For finite-dimensional history spaces over fixed finite horizons, we distinguish two minimality problems. Reachable task quotients determine the minimum state dimension for preserving prescribed future tasks on reachable histories. Backward invariant envelopes characterize the minimum dimension of exact linear realizations recovering prescribed analyses on full history spaces within the admissible class. The minimum number of additional independent state directions is given by the rank of the propagated closure defect operator restricted to the kernel of the current analysis. For geometrically weighted countable histories, matrix mode transport yields structured exact recurrences and a uniform exponential decay estimate for state transitions. Additional conditions provide uniform Gram bounds and refined decay estimates. A stationary Meixner specialization yields explicit recurrence matrices, an O(N) arithmetic state update, and minimum augmentation dimensions over finite horizons for selected coefficients. Numerical experiments examine recurrence accuracy, state transition bounds, Gram conditions, and minimum realization dimensions.

papers.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
papers.abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean, which machine-checks the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem. Both the interval certification and formalization were developed with substantial assistance from a large language model, while the validity of the result remains independent of the language model: the numerical bounds are rigorously enclosed by interval arithmetic and the subsequent mathematical deductions are checked by the Lean kernel. Together, these steps provide a pipeline from neural discovery to rigorous numerical certification and machine-checked verification with auditable mathematical guarantees.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz-type involving the Riesz potential $$ u(x)=\ell+C_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{u(y)(|\nabla u(y)|^{2}+|u_k(y)|^2)-u_k(y)e_k}{|x-y|^{n-α}}dy, $$ where $\ell \in \mathbb{R}^k$ is a constant vector, $C_* \neq 0$ is a constant, $u\colon\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{S}^{k-1}:=\{u=(u_1,u_2,\cdots,u_k) \in {\mathbb{R}^{k}};|u|=1\}$, $k \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$, and $0<α<n$. We provide a decay rate at which $|u_k|$ converges to zero under some mild conditions. This argument still works for the Ginzburg-Landau-type integral equation.

papers.title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $Ω_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $Ω_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.

papers.title: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
papers.abstract: Controlling nonclassical light while maintaining a finite cavity response requires selective suppression of unwanted multiphoton excitation. We investigate a ring-cavity system containing two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, where electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) provides resonant access to a dark-state polariton. The exchange interaction shifts the polariton resonance while modifying the dressed two-photon excitation pathways. Strong photon antibunching emerges when the one-polariton resonance nearly coincides with a destructive-interference minimum of the second-photon transition amplitude. By jointly tuning the exchange interaction and control-field strength, pronounced photon blockade with a finite intracavity population can be sustained over an extended interaction range. We further show that the relative cavity-coupling phase redistributes optical coupling between symmetric and antisymmetric collective channels with opposite exchange shifts, allowing the photon statistics to switch between antibunching and bunching at fixed exchange strength. This mechanism provides a possible route to tunable nonclassical-light sources based on coherent control of collective excitation pathways.

papers.title: Scalar curvature bounds and rigidity of Ricci shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton of dimension at least two is a finite quotient of an Einstein cylinder if its scalar curvature is bounded below by the cylindrical value. The corresponding pointwise strict bound implies compactness. We also establish one-endedness criteria using curvature information at critical points of the potential, including degenerate ones, and obtain sharp one-endedness and rigidity results under global Ricci norm bounds.

papers.title: Preservation and Loss of Log-Concavity in the Repulsive Vlasov--Poisson System
papers.abstract: Prékopa's theorem shows that, for jointly log-concave initial data, free transport preserves the log-concavity of spatial densities. This paper asks whether this property persists in the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system. In dimensions two and higher, we construct smooth, strongly log-concave initial distributions whose spatial densities lose log-concavity at arbitrarily small positive times. For one-dimensional cold-ion data, we prove that the spatial density remains log-concave for all time.

papers.title: Non-symmetric integral geometry: alternative reconstruction procedure with dual Radon transform
papers.abstract: In the note, we use the principles of non-symmetric integral geometry (non-integral geometry), related to the non-symmetric restricted integration measure, to extend the well-known relations traced from the Fourier slice theorem and the dual Radon transform. The proposed generalization is a very useful for the alternative restoration of the outset function. The latter impacts entirely on the image reconstruction process. The derived relations confirm the complexity of the inversion operator thanks for the symmetry breaking of integration measure.

papers.title: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments
papers.abstract: Quantifying the interactivity of quantum instruments is fundamental to understanding their resource structure and operational capabilities. Here, we introduce the interactive weight of quantum instruments as a resource quantifier that measures the minimum fraction of an instrument that cannot be explained by non-interactive components. Through quantum-information tasks including quantum-state recovery, positive linear loss games, and environment-assisted input-blind extraction, we establish quantitative bounds on the interactive weight of quantum instruments and exact operational characterizations of its complementary quantity, the maximal non-interactive content. In particular, we extend environment-assisted input-blind extraction to the setting of restricted environmental access and develop a corresponding framework. Within the allowed-operations framework introduced by Hsieh et al., we establish fundamental resource-theoretic properties of the interactive weight of quantum instruments, including faithfulness, convexity, and monotonicity under deterministic allowed operations. Furthermore, we prove that the maximal non-interactive content satisfies exact multiplicativity under independent parallel composition, yielding necessary constraints on multicopy resource conversion and establishing the finite-copy maximal-weight distillation no-go result under deterministic allowed operations. These results establish a unified theoretical framework for the interactive weight of quantum instruments from the perspectives of resource quantification, operational interpretation, and resource conversion, providing systematic theoretical tools for the quantitative comparison and conversion of interactive quantum instruments.

papers.title: A Partial-Matching Proof of the Neyman--Pearson Lemma
papers.abstract: Testing seeks to distinguish distributions, whereas matching seeks to identify their common mass. I show that this apparent opposition provides a direct proof of the Neyman--Pearson lemma. Maximal partial matching between the alternative distribution and a scaled null distribution separates them into a common component and two mutually singular residuals. An elementary dual problem then turns this separation into a testing rule: complementary slackness forces rejection on the alternative residual and non-rejection on the scaled-null residual, leaving freedom to randomize at the likelihood-ratio threshold. Thus the optimal test emerges from maximal matching rather than being proposed in advance. The matching profile also determines the optimal power envelope.

papers.title: The $q$-Poincaré sum and separability in a Coxeter group
papers.abstract: Given a finite Coxeter group $W$ and an element $q$ of a commutative ring $\mathbf{k}$, we define the element $\mathbf{L}_{q} :=\sum_{w\in W}q^{\ell\left( w\right) }w$ of its group algebra $\mathbf{k}\left[ W\right] $. We say that an element $w\in W$ is $W$\emph{-length-symmetric} if its coefficient in the commutator $\left[ \mathbf{L}_{a},\mathbf{L}_{b}\right] $ is $0$ for all $\mathbf{k}$ and all $a,b\in\mathbf{k}$. We prove several sufficient criteria for elements to be $W$-length-symmetric. In particular, we show that any separable permutation (i.e., permutation avoiding the patterns $2413$ and $3142$) in the symmetric group $S_{n}$ is $S_{n}$-length-symmetric. More generally, we construct a notion of separable elements of a finite Coxeter group $W$ (which, for finite Weyl groups, agrees with the eponymous notion introduced by Gaetz and Gao), and show that all such elements are $W$-length-symmetric. This is only a sufficient condition; other $W$-length-symmetric elements include (twisted) involutions and elements of dihedral parabolic subgroups.

papers.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. We show that the equation residuals retain this decomposition form, allowing high-dimensional loss integrals to be evaluated through combinations of one-dimensional integrals. The resulting computational and storage costs are reduced from exponential to polynomial growth with dimension. To improve the prediction accuracy in the high-field limit, we enhance the baseline AP loss by incorporating the first moment equation. The added loss term directly constrains the limiting flux closure to reduce its approximation error in the high-field regime. The enhanced AP loss can still be evaluated dimension-wise. Numerical results show that APTNN improves prediction accuracy in the high-field regime with significantly reduced computational costs and memory usage. For a 3D3V VPFP problem with multiple random inputs, training takes less than 30 minutes on a single GPU.

papers.title: Continuous-time q-Learning for Finite-Horizon Portfolio Choice with Optimal Stopping in Jump-Diffusion Markets
papers.abstract: We develop a structured continuous-time q-learning framework for finite-horizon investment and optimal stopping under jump-diffusion dynamics with unknown parameters. A penalty approximation transforms the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality into an HJB equation with a binary control for the stopping penalty. An auxiliary state incorporates the resulting control-dependent discount factor into a Markovian formulation. We randomize controls on the mixed action space and introduce Shannon entropy regularization, establishing policy improvement and martingale characterizations of the continuous-time q-function. These results motivate a structured q-learning algorithm that constructs the q-function from the penalty HJB equation and jointly learns the value function and unknown generator parameters from sample paths. We apply the method to portfolio choice with optimal stopping in a simulation study. We further conduct a two-asset empirical study, evaluating learned strategies on bootstrap paths from held-out test returns versus an MLE-finite difference benchmark.

papers.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
papers.abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

papers.title: Infinitely many nonradial positive solutions for two-coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations in $\bbr^N$ without symmetry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the following two-coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations: \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} &-Δu+P(x)u=μu^3+βuv^2,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &-Δv+Q(x)v=νv^3+βu^2v,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &u,\,v\in H^1(\R^N) \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $N=2,3$, $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are potentials, $μ$ and $ν$ are positive coefficients and $β\in\R\setminus\{0\}$ is the coupling parameter. By developing the intermediate reduction arguments in [del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015], we prove the existence of infinitely many nonradial positive solutions to the above system under suitable regularity and decay conditions on $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$, {\bf but without any symmetry assumptions on them}. The scalar version of our result also gives {\bf a positive answer} to the first part of [Question~3, del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015] and our method might be helpful in studying other problems.

papers.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition. Our approach uses increasing chains, introduced by Sottile for the one-row case, and builds on the skew Schubert functions studied by Bergeron and Sottile. The key step is to connect increasing chains and these functions with the parallel classes of positroid varieties.

papers.title: Finite-Support Approximation in Variable-Coefficient Sobolev Spaces on Nonhomogeneous Flow-Measure Trees
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a nonhomogeneous rooted tree equipped with a positive flow measure $m$. For $1<p<\infty$, consider the variable-coefficient Sobolev space on the nonhomogeneous flow-measure tree~$T$ \[ W_a^{1,p}(T,m) = \left\{ f\in L^p(T,m): \sum_{x\ne ρ}a(x)m(x)\lvert f(x)-f(π(x))\rvert^p<\infty \right\}, \] where $a$ is a positive variable coefficient, $ρ$ denotes the root and $π(x)$ denotes the parent of $x$. Using an averaging method over descendant levels, we prove the density of finitely supported functions in $W_a^{1,p}(T,m)$ for coefficients satisfying a weighted moment condition. As an application, the relationship between solutions on finite domains and global solutions is clarified for $p=2$.

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA is governed by rank, which controls parameter budget and locally accessible task updates. Existing dynamic-rank methods mainly focus on capacity allocation, leaving unresolved whether the current adaptation space is sufficient for the task. We characterize the first-order information boundary of standard factor gradients, showing that their unobservable subspace coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold. Thus, factor gradients alone cannot distinguish under-optimization within the current space from task-relevant directions beyond its first-order reach. This motivates a geometric view of rank evolution, where tangent information optimizes existing degrees of freedom and the normal spectrum quantifies the value of new ones. Under a local quadratic model, we show that leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion, with spectral energy determining its gain. Building on this characterization, we propose GEAR, which turns the tangent--normal decomposition into rank evolution through tangent-space optimization, matrix-free normal-spectrum estimation for rank expansion, and task-induced geometric initialization. Across language and vision benchmarks, GEAR achieves the best average performance in all evaluated settings with substantially fewer trainable parameters. On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

papers.title: Boltzmann equations with dilatation and shear: global well-posedness and stability
papers.abstract: We study global well-posedness and stability for Boltzmann equations with linear velocity deformation, allowing for arbitrarily large deformation strength. For diagonal dilatation with $-2<γ\leq0$ and cylindrical dilatation with $-3/2<γ\leq0$, with or without shear, we construct global homogeneous solutions for small data and prove their stability under small spatially inhomogeneous perturbations. In scaled variables, the perturbations remain uniformly controlled in deformation-adapted spaces and decay in mixed spatial--velocity norms, algebraically in the diagonal regime and exponentially in the cylindrical regime. For homogeneous simple shear with $-2\leqγ\leq0$, we prove global existence and uniqueness for nonnegative data with finite mass and Fisher information, without smallness or a finite-energy assumption. These solutions conserve mass and propagate additional Sobolev regularity. For spatially inhomogeneous simple shear with $-2<γ\leq0$, we establish global well-posedness for small data. The analysis combines commuting vector fields, dispersive and bilinear collision estimates, and integrability of the rescaled collision coefficients. For homogeneous shear, a positivity-preserving splitting transfers Fisher-information control to rough data, while a Lorentz-space estimate includes the endpoint $γ=-2$ in the global continuation argument.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods for Unbounded Problems
papers.abstract: Last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient methods have attracted significant attention as practical implementations typically return the last iterate instead of an average of the iterates. In this paper, we study two approaches for analyzing the last-iterate convergence of proximal and projected stochastic gradient methods without bounded domain or bounded variance assumptions, where black-box variational inference serves as a running example. Under two related assumptions relaxing the bounded variance, we show near-optimal anytime rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the last iterate. Moreover, when the horizon $T$ is known, we remove the logarithmic factor and obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$, matching the order known under bounded variance or bounded domain assumptions.

papers.title: On explicit units in a family of cubic fields and the arithmetic of curves arising from powers of these units
papers.abstract: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $K_b$ be the cubic field generated by the unique real root of $x^3-3bx-b^3$, let $η_0$ be its fundamental unit, and let $η_b$ be the explicit unit studied in the companion paper (arXiv:2609.37389). Write $η_b=η_0^{n(b)}$. Deciding whether $n(b)$ is divisible by $q$ amounts to finding the integral points of a plane curve $C_q$ of degree $2q$. We prove that for every integer $q\ge1$ the curve $C_q$ is irreducible with $g(C_q)=\binom{q-1}{2}$, the genus of a smooth plane curve of degree $q$ rather than of degree $2q$. The proof is not a genus computation but a structural one: $C_q$ is the inverse image, under the $q$-power map of a two-dimensional torus, of the curve traced by the minimal polynomial of $η_b$ as $b$ varies, and the formula falls out of two applications of Riemann-Hurwitz in the resulting tower. As a consequence the problem splits into exactly three regimes: $q=2$ rational, $q=3$ elliptic, and $q\ge4$ of general type. In particular only finitely many $b$ have $q\mid n(b)$ for each $q\ge4$. A lower bound for linear forms in two logarithms gives $n(b)<6082138$ for every $b$, so $n(b)\in\{1,2\}$ for all but finitely many $b$, though not effectively. We add two computations: $n(b)$ is determined outright for $|b|\le10^{30}$, and the rational points of $C_4$ are determined by quadratic Chabauty, giving $4\mid n(b)\iff b\in\{-75,-3,5,96\}$. We state precisely which parts of the latter rest on certified arithmetic and which do not. Finally, we show that $K_b\cong K_{b'}$ with $b\neq b'$ holds for $\{b,b'\}=\{-1,5\}$, and otherwise only if one of the two parameters, $c$ say, satisfies $|c|>10^{30}$ and $n(c)$ is divisible by a prime $q\ge5$. There are only finitely many such pairs.

papers.title: Sobolev homeomorphisms and Jordan curves with positive area
papers.abstract: Each homeomorphic parametrization of a Jordan curve via the unit circle $\mathbb{S}\subset \mathbb{S}^2$ extends to a homeomorphism of the entire $\mathbb{S}^2.$ We show that there exists a Jordan curve of positive area whose every parametrization via $\mathbb{S}$ admits a homeomorphic extension that has $p$-Sobolev regularity on $\mathbb{S}^2$ for all exponents $1\le p<2 .$ This is obtained via a new sharp extension result for the case of $p<2.$

papers.title: A true $Π^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $Π^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehatφ$ denotes its interpretation on $ω$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehatφ$ is a $Π^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

papers.title: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions
papers.abstract: We exhibit a total Boolean function on n input bits whose bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (and hence one-way) communication complexity is in O(\sqrt n), whereas its randomised one-way (and hence simultaneous-message) communication complexity is in Ω(n). The same function admits a classical simultaneous-message protocol of cost O(\sqrt n) when the players share O(\sqrt n) EPR pairs.

papers.title: On the number of edges in quasiplanar graphs
papers.abstract: A $k$-quasiplanar graph is a graph drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. Pach, Shahrokhi, and Szegedy conjectured that every such graph on $n$ vertices has $O_k(n)$ edges. ChatGPT produced a proof of this conjecture. Here, we present a simplified, self-contained version of that proof.

papers.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
papers.abstract: We prove weak well-posedness for the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion that is Holder continuous of any positive order. This resolves the weak uniqueness problem in the full positive Holder range, extending our earlier result for exponents above two thirds (arXiv:2608.01279). The proof couples a weak solution to a smooth companion and uses spatial cancellation to estimate the signed covariance difference in a negative Sobolev norm. A finite Gaussian expansion on each Littlewood-Paley block gives the decay needed to remove the coupling drift by a change of measure. A localized Girsanov argument extends the result to measurable drifts of linear growth.

papers.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
papers.abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schrödingerization
papers.abstract: The decomplexification procedure establishes a mathematical equivalence between finite dimensional quantum dynamics and classical dynamics by mapping the complex quantum domain onto the real classical one. Its inverse process, complexification --- which lifts a classical dynamics to an equivalent quantum formulation --- is of great interest, particularly because it enables the quantum simulation of equations that are of classical relevance. In this way, one can prepare the solution of classical differential equations to be implemented using quantum computation tools. In the present work, we recall the decomplexification procedure and also discuss several distinct strategies for performing the complexification of classical equations, so as to obtain the corresponding quantum-equivalent dynamics.

papers.title: Compressions of Linear Relations in Krein Spaces
papers.abstract: Given an orthogonal decomposition \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{H}[\dotplus]\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) of a Krein space, we study compressions \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)\) of linear relations \(R\) in \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}}\) to \(\mathfrak{H}\). We formulate a sufficient condition that ensures that compression commutes with taking adjoints, that is, the adjoint identity \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R^{\widetilde{*}}) = {\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)^{*}\) holds. We derive preservation and reflection results for the compression of maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint linear relations. For nonnegative linear relations, the adjoint identity also implies that compression commutes with taking the Friedrichs extension. For \(\mathfrak{H}\ne\{0\}\), we characterize finite dimensionality of the exit space \(\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) by universal compression properties. Finally, we give a criterion for the adjoint identity to hold in terms of bounded linear functionals on \(R\).

papers.title: Ultrahomogeneous hypertournaments
papers.abstract: A $k$-hypertournament is a higher-arity generalisation of a tournament, consisting of a set together with an irreflexive $k$-ary relation such that the automorphism group of each substructure of size $k$ is the alternating group $\mathrm{A}_k$. We show that, for each $k \geq 3$, there are continuum-many non-isomorphic countable ultrahomogeneous $k$-hypertournaments, answering a question of Cherlin.

papers.title: Rational Turán exponents of a single $k$-uniform hypergraph
papers.abstract: For a fixed $k$-uniform hypergraph $F$, let $\mathrm{ex}_k(n,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $F$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that for every integer $k\ge2$ and every rational $r\in[0,1]$ there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph $F_{k,r}$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathrm{ex}_k(n,F_{k,r})=Θ(n^{k-r}). \end{equation*} The case $k=2$ is the rational exponents conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits \cite{Erdos1988}, also known as Erdős problem \#571 \cite{BloomErdoswebsite}; a proof was announced in September 2026 and is expounded by Conlon et al.\ \cite{Conlon-Janzer-Jiang-Kim-Lee-Liu-Longbrake-Yepremyan}. For $k\ge3$ the theorem extends their result to $k$-uniform hypergraphs. In the single-hypergraph setting, this strengthens Fitch's finite-family theorem \cite{Fitch} by realizing each exponent with a single forbidden $k$-uniform hypergraph for $0\le r\le1$. We also show, via an explicit two-edge construction, that for $k\ge4$ this strengthening fails for $\lceil k/2\rceil<r\le k-1$: no single $k$-uniform hypergraph $F$ then satisfies $\mathrm{ex}_k(n,F)=Θ(n^{k-r})$. The main result of this paper has been formalized in Lean 4, conditional on two explicitly stated axioms.

papers.title: Unifying First-Order Coherence, Concurrence, and Bell Correlations in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
papers.abstract: Neutrino oscillations provide a natural setting for investigating the quantum character of flavor conversion and the distribution of quantum resources over macroscopic distances. Here, we study exact relations among purity-based first-order coherence, pairwise concurrence, and the maximal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) value in coherent three-flavor neutrino oscillations. By expressing the evolving neutrino as a three-qubit single-excitation state, we derive the generally mixed two-qubit reductions and show that the squared first-order coherence of each flavor mode and its two associated squared concurrences sum to unity. Furthermore, a closed two-branch relation is obtained, showing that the maximal CHSH value of any reduced pair is determined by its average first-order coherence and concurrence. The branch structure follows from the correlation-tensor spectrum and yields exact conditions for CHSH violation. For the vacuum parameters and propagation ranges considered, electron preparation gives weak CHSH violations in electroncontaining pairs, while muon preparation produces a dominant utau pair with substantially stronger concurrence and Bell correlations. The comparison also identifies the thirdflavor contribution responsible for the different locations of concurrence and CHSH maxima. These results clarify the distribution of quantum correlations during flavor evolution and provide a basis for extensions to coherent matter propagation and wave-packet-induced mixed states.

papers.title: Degree profiles of uniform polynomial consequences: Linear lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus
papers.abstract: This paper proves asymptotically optimal linear degree lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus, yielding a four-way polynomial-versus-exponential proof-size classification for uniform polynomial consequences over fields of positive characteristic. The size bounds use full, explicit coefficient lists, including zeros. Apart from a fixed finite initial range, exactly one of four cases occurs: $\mathrm T_1$, bounded degree; $\mathrm T_2$, degree at least linear in the universe size $n$; $\mathrm T_3$, constant degree on some residue classes and at least linear degree on the others; or $\mathrm T_4$, infinitely many recurring finite degrees, with bounded-degree subsequences and finite $Ω(n)$ peaks at arbitrarily large sizes. Thus the size patterns are polynomial bounds, exponential lower bounds, a periodic mixture, or polynomial subsequences with finite exponential peaks, respectively. Underivable targets have degree $\infty$, and both proof systems assign the same type. The result strengthens my 2008--2009 refutation classification and extends it to uniform consequences. The proof uses degree-preserving lifting with onset and period bounds linear in the degree. A common $p$-adic hardness spectrum describes the four types topologically. Distinguishing any two types is undecidable already for refutations. The linear degree bounds, four-way classification and pairwise undecidability results have been formalised and verified in Lean. The Lean formalisation, verification records and an accompanying tutorial are available in the supporting materials (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23965838).

papers.title: Minimum-Time Interceptor Selection and Obstacle-Avoiding Path Planning for Heterogeneous UAVs
papers.abstract: Selecting the most suitable unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to intercept a moving target is challenging when multiple vehicles have different speeds, initial headings, turning capabilities and launch delays, particularly in environments containing obstacles. This paper develops a computationally efficient framework that integrates minimum-time interceptor selection with obstacle-avoiding path planning for heterogeneous UAVs. The interception problem for each UAV is formulated as a minimum-time optimal control problem and solved numerically using an arc-parameterised nonlinear programming model based on Dubins-type paths. The candidate trajectories consist of minimum-radius circular arcs, straight-line segments and tangential obstacle-boundary arcs, with exact geometric distance constraints imposed to ensure obstacle avoidance along the entire path. To improve computational efficiency, a closed-form lower bound on interception time is incorporated into a bound-and-select algorithm that eliminates UAVs unable to improve the best verified feasible interception time. The proposed pruning strategy preserves the best computed interception decision obtained through full enumeration while reducing computational effort. Numerical experiments investigate the effects of target speed, UAV turning radius, launch delay and obstacle configuration. Across 20 randomly generated scenarios involving up to eight UAVs, the proposed approach reduces average computational time by approximately 85$\%$ for eight-vehicle teams without changing the selected interceptor or its computed interception time. The proposed approach provides an efficient method for selecting a single UAV and generating feasible Dubins-type interception trajectories in obstacle-constrained environments.

papers.title: Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
papers.abstract: We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with càdlàg trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. The proof combines the jump Itô formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. Under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for few-copy Gaussian tomography, and the absence of a fermionic warm regime
papers.abstract: Chen, Mele, Mele and Preskill proved a crossover for bosonic Gaussian tomography: cold states need $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ copies under single-copy or few-copy measurements, warm ones $Θ(m^2/ε^2)$. The author proved $Ω(m^3/ε^2)$ for adaptive single-copy tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states. This note shows the crossover has no fermionic counterpart and extends the fermionic bound to blocks of $k$ copies. There is no warm regime: on the quadratic Gibbs balls $β\|h\|_F\leβ_0$ of unknown Hamiltonian $h$, the single-copy rate is $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ for every fixed $β_0>0$, at accuracies that resolve the ball, with a lower-bound constant independent of $β_0$. At the maximally mixed state a replicated-parameter Fisher budget gives $N>m^3/(8{,}553{,}600\,k\,ε^2)$ for blocks of at most $k$ copies and all $ε\le1/3600$; an exact formula for the maximal block Fisher information, via spinor tensor powers of $\mathfrak{so}(2m)$, shows that the budget $mt^2$ behind it is asymptotically attained for every fixed block size; whether $1/k$ is the true rate is open. Near the vacuum, block protocols need $Ω(m^3/(ε^2\min\{\sqrt k,m\}))$ copies, with no logarithm, via an exterior-power embedding of qudit tomography; parity superselection changes no rate, and number superselection costs nothing on number-conserving inputs. The embedding also carries upper bounds: a particle-number measurement followed by the $k$-copy qudit protocol of Nayak and Zhou attains the lower bound for every $k$ on number-conserving fermionic Gaussian states with bounded fugacity trace and on passive bosonic Gaussian states with bounded photon number, and a heterodyne stage that undoes displacement and squeezing extends this to all cold bosonic Gaussian states. This closes their $k$-entangled gap on the cold class; intermediate temperatures remain open.

papers.title: Cubic Optimization over Three Nonnegative Integers Is NP-hard
papers.abstract: We prove that deciding whether an integer cubic polynomial takes a value at most one over three nonnegative integers is NP-hard. Hardness holds even when every feasible objective value is a positive integer, so every constructed instance has a finite, attained minimum. This establishes a sharp dimension boundary for the tractability of cubic integer optimization in fixed dimension. Our reduction from positive 1-in-3 satisfiability encodes Boolean constraints as modular conditions and uses an algebraic norm to construct a cubic objective whose minimum is one exactly for satisfiable formulas. The resulting six-parameter threshold language is NP-complete and admits short exponent certificates.

papers.title: Pattern avoidance classes of parking permutations with fixed lucky sets
papers.abstract: For a parking function, the resulting sequence after all cars have parked is called the associated parking permutation. For each parking function, cars that park in their preferred spot are called lucky cars. In this paper, we enumerate parking permutations that avoid a specified set of permutation patterns in $\mathfrak{S}_3$ and whose lucky cars are the first $k$ cars. Often, the enumeration simplifies to a product of a fraction with a binomial coefficient, recovering existing sequences in the OEIS. For two of the classes, the enumerations are new sequences.

papers.title: Quadratic Extractors
papers.abstract: A quadratic source is a random variable $X\sim\mathbb{F}_2^n$ generated by applying $n$ quadratics to a hidden uniform string. Previously, the best-known explicit extractor for this model required min-entropy roughly $k=n-\sqrt{\log n}$. In this paper, we give an explicit construction for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$. Even for the special case of $2$-local sources, where each bit of $X$ depends on two hidden uniform bits, achieving an entropy requirement below $k=\sqrt{n}$ was an important open problem. This is because such sources provably cannot be reduced (in a black-box manner) to our most powerful general-purpose seedless extractor, known as a sumset extractor. Our new extractor bypasses this barrier, providing the first explicit construction to go beyond sumset extraction.

papers.title: Higher Noncommutative Motives and Higher K-theory
papers.abstract: We construct higher additive noncommutative motives of stable $(\infty,n)$-categories, extending the additive motives of Blumberg, Gepner, and Tabuada and the secondary theory of Mazel-Gee and Stern. We formulate a notion of exact sequences and establish the universal property of the resulting additive motives. We give two equivalent constructions: a localization of enriched presheaves and a weighted Waldhausen $S$-construction on complete exact flags. We then compute their Hom objects, obtaining ordinary K-theory at the first level and lower additive motives recursively at higher levels. Our results recover the classical and secondary theories, provide coherent multiplicative structures, and yield an endofunctor on the category of Stefanich rings. In short, higher motives are higher K-theory.

papers.title: Fields Generated by a Single Point on Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We study the finite extensions of a number field generated by a single point on an elliptic curve. We construct geometrically non-isomorphic elliptic curves with complex multiplication that generate the same collection of extensions, giving a negative answer to a question of Mazur and Rubin. For torsion-generated fields, we prove that inclusion of the collections up to finitely many exceptions implies isogeny over the ground field, and in the non-CM case even isomorphism. When all geometric endomorphisms are defined over the ground field, we characterize equality of the torsion-generated collections by the existence, for every prime $p$, of an isogeny over the ground field of degree prime to $p$. This condition also implies equality of the full collections of fields generated by a single point.

papers.title: Values of differentials of plane branches: block decomposition and semiroots
papers.abstract: We study the passage of special gaps from a Zariski semiroot to a plane branch. A decomposition into rectangular blocks allows us to compute the maximal valuations of the coefficients of differentials and describe the image of the transition map. We treat vertical and horizontal decompositions, as well as decompositions with alternations, obtaining criteria for the preservation of special gaps. For towers whose ramification indices after the first are all equal to two, the value semigroup of the branch and the special gaps of the first semiroot determine the special gaps of the branch.

papers.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
papers.abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.

papers.title: $s$-quasi-transitive weakly distance-regular digraphs
papers.abstract: A digraph is $s$-quasi-transitive if, for every path $(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_s)$ of length $s$, either $(x_0,x_s)\in AΓ$ or $(x_s,x_0)\in AΓ$ (or both). In this paper, we give a characterization of $s$-quasi-transitive commutative weakly distance-regular digraphs, where $s=4$, or $s\geq 5$ and the cycle polar diameter is at least $s$.

papers.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
papers.abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4π^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

papers.title: Exact penalties for maximum-edge bicliques in bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given a bipartite graph $G$, we denote by $g(G)$ the largest product $|A||B|$ over pairs of vertex sets $A$ and $B$, one on each side, with no edge between them. These pairs are the bicliques of the bipartite complement of $G$; hence, computing $g(G)$ is the maximum-edge biclique problem, which is NP-hard, as shown by Peeters in 2003. Gillis and Glineur characterized it by a continuous quadratic program, in which a large enough penalty on the edges of $G$ makes the global maximizers correspond to the maximum pairs and the local maximizers to the maximal ones. We propose a new threshold for the penalty, which depends only on $g(G)$. For any penalty at or above it, the global maximizers correspond exactly to the maximum pairs, and every local maximizer with positive value corresponds to a maximal pair. This threshold is never larger than theirs and is sharp up to an additive $1/2$. Spectral and semidefinite bounds give computable penalties; in experiments, a simple local ascent succeeds far more often with the semidefinite one than with the earlier thresholds, although on our graphs that bound already reveals $g(G)$. The penalty formulation, whose optimal value is $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, is also a copositive formulation of $g(G)$. Strengthening a semidefinite bound of Laurent, Polak and Vargas with the completely positive cone gives exactly $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$, while the doubly nonnegative strengthening is already inexact on six vertices. Finally, Pólya's linear programming approximations of the copositive cone become finite at an explicit level and converge to $\sqrt{g(G)}/2$ without ever being exact.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for monotone factors of smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We prove that a transitive monotone factor of a smooth surface diffeomorphism has a unique measure of maximal entropy whenever its topological entropy is positive. Its entropy is the entropy of a single homoclinic class of the diffeomorphism, and the factor map is a measure-theoretic isomorphism on every ergodic measure with positive entropy of that class. The other homoclinic classes are mapped to periodic orbits. We give an application to the essential factor of a diffeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map ---possibly relative to a finite invariant set--- constructed by García-Sassi \& Tal: the essential factor has a unique measure of maximal entropy, which is Bernoulli and has full support.

papers.title: Extending a property of vector spaces to abelian groups
papers.abstract: In this note, we determine the finite abelian groups $G$ such that for every subgroup $H\leq G$ there exists an automorphism $f\in{\rm Aut}(G)$ with ${\rm Fix}(f)=H$. This provides a partial answer to a problem posed by Deaconescu and Walls. Two generalizations of this problem are also proposed.

papers.title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}, \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(σ, ε)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates among observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a data-driven threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule allows lower thresholds to retain more observations for testing while limiting size distortions, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: A Complete Equational Theory for Quantum Circuits with Generalized Control
papers.abstract: Controlled subcircuits are commonplace in quantum algorithms as they represent the quantum analogue of branching statements (if then). We introduce a generalization of controlled subcircuits in the form of a binary operation which sends pairs of unitary quantum circuits to a generalized controlled operation, whose semantics are based on matrix exponentials and logarithms. The family of quantum circuits with generalized controlled operations and circuit exponentiation is denoted HQC for Hierarchical Quantum Circuits. We formalize HQC as a modified prop category using a novel category-theoretic construction, and provide a sound and complete equational theory for diagrammatic reasoning in HQC.

papers.title: On Packed Passenger Permutations
papers.abstract: An occupied seat in a binary row is called packed if both of its immediate neighbors are occupied. We give a self-contained combinatorial account of this statistic, equivalently the number of overlapping occurrences of 111. An occupied-block decomposition yields a coefficient formula at fixed occupancy and a direct proof of the sharp minimum max{0,3m-2n-2} for m passengers in n seats, including arrangements attaining the bound. The same decomposition gives a rational generating function, recurrences, expectations, and avoidance asymptotics. Full rows, in which every empty seat would become packed upon being filled, are related to independent sets of a path. A neighborhood-union expansion also gives exact counts on rectangular grids. The emphasis is a unified elementary presentation and explicit extremal constructions, rather than a new general enumeration method.

papers.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
papers.abstract: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.

papers.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)Δu =|u|^{p-2}u+μu &\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_Ω|u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $μ\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass. We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(Ω)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.

papers.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $Φ$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $Ω(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $Φ_{\rm p}(d)=Θ(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le Φ_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $Φ_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $Φ_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[Φ_{\rm d},Φ_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.

papers.title: Thermally-driven quantum reservoir computing
papers.abstract: Heat generation limits computation, classical and quantum, from single logic gates to entire data centers. However, an in principle limiting physical factor can sometimes be turned into a resource. In reservoir computing, energy dissipation is what gives a reservoir its fading memory. Here, we introduce a paradigm where the data injection itself is encoded on the time-dependent temperature of a thermal bath. We derive an exact expression for the nonlinear response of any fixed readout, and prove a rigorous memory-nonlinearity trade-off which turns out to be a structural necessity, rather than a tunable dynamical regime, since the same coupling that injects data also enforces equilibration. We illustrate both results with a driven qubit, using a single free parameter, and with a pair of coupled qubits, where the breaking of a discrete symmetry opens a fifteen-dimensional space to a single observable, yet that observable alone recovers just over half of it. This refutes the misconception that large Hilbert spaces guarantee computational power. Our results relocate the memory-nonlinearity trade-off from the reservoir's dynamics to its measurement channel, pointing to observable choice and bath engineering (instead of Hamiltonian control) as the physical levers for a thermally-native quantum reservoir computer.

papers.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
papers.abstract: We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<α<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $σ\partial_xF\ge0$, $σQ\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α/2}$. In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-α/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-α/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of Bénilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-α})$. This bound takes the place of the Oleĭnik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-α/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
papers.abstract: Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of $\varepsilon$-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open. We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium for every $\varepsilon > 0$, provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is $\{0,1\}^{\dN}$ endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration. Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, for every $\varepsilon > 0$. The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.

papers.title: On Amoebas and the Arithmetic Rigidity of the Mahler Measure
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric rigidity theory for Mahler measure based on the global structure of Ronkin functions and amoebas. Our starting point is the theorem of Ronkin describing the affine linearity of the Ronkin function on the complement of the amoeba and the identification of its gradients with lattice points of the Newton polytope. Combining this deep analytic input with convex duality and toric geometry, we show that the vanishing of the Mahler measure is an extremal phenomenon: it occurs if and only if the Ronkin function collapses to the piecewise linear support function of the Newton polytope. This collapse forces a degeneration of the amoeba onto the $(n\!-\!1)$-skeleton of a toric fan and implies that the zero locus of the polynomial is contained in a translate of a codimension-one subtorus. As a first application of this rigidity principle, we recover the generalized Kronecker theorem characterizing Laurent polynomials of vanishing Mahler measure. Our approach bypasses the classical Boyd--Lawton limit formulas and replaces analytic projection arguments by a global convex-geometric and potential-theoretic mechanism rooted in the geometry of amoebas.

papers.title: On a Dual Heterotic Kodaira-Spencer Theory
papers.abstract: We consider a dual version of heterotic Kodaira-Spencer theory on a Calabi-Yau three-fold $X$ with background fluxes, related to the type I BCOV theory of Costello-Li. We implement the Green-Schwarz mechanism of Costello-Li, where the Beltrami differential plays the role of the Green-Schwarz field. On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.

papers.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers II. Rational Maps
papers.abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked which analytic functions map the set $\mathscr L$ of Liouville numbers into itself. In the first paper of this series, we proved that every real-analytic solution on an open interval is the restriction of a real rational function. We now identify a canonical subfield $\mathbb L$ of $\mathbb R$ such that, for every nonconstant $R\in\mathbb R(X)$ and every nonempty open interval $I$ in its domain, $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathscr L$ if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$ and $R^{-1}(\mathbb Q)\cap I\cap\mathscr L=\varnothing$. The weaker inclusion $R(I\cap\mathscr L)\subseteq\mathbb Q\cup\mathscr L$ holds if and only if $R$ is defined over $\mathbb L$. If $R$ is not defined over $\mathbb L$, every such interval contains a Cantor set of Liouville numbers whose images under $R$ are irrational and have irrationality exponents bounded by a constant depending only on $R$. We also construct continuum many positive strong Liouville numbers $σ$ for which $σX^m$ preserves $\mathscr L$ for every $m\geq2$, with all nonzero rational fibers consisting of $U_m$-numbers.

papers.title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
papers.abstract: Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising pathway to scale superconducting quantum hardware, but restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity creates a major transpilation bottleneck. Current DQC transpilation methods often assume idealized hardware connectivity, ignore subsequent intra-module routing, or suffer from substantial computational overheads that limit their applicability at scale. To address this, we introduce a scalable transpilation method tailored for the restricted connectivity of distributed superconducting quantum architectures. Specifically, our quantum interaction graph (QIG) approach couples a graph-partitioning mapping step with a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic. On a 48-qubit (3 QPUs $\times$ 16 qubits) architecture with all-to-all inter-core connectivity, our method reduces average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% (unstructured) and 24.01% (structured), while delivering >250$\times$ speed-ups for structured workloads compared to the state-of-the-art DMapS algorithm. On the 399-qubit (3$\times$133) IBM Flamingo, where DMapS times out on dense circuits, our approach maintains practical runtimes. Against a DQC-adapted SABRE baseline, it reduces structured circuit routing costs by up to 51.94% (all-to-all inter-core topology) and 51.96% (restricted line topology). Ultimately, this work delivers a practical transpilation method for DQC at scale.

papers.title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
papers.abstract: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,Γ)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},π_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): Γ(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.

papers.title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+Δu+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $ω\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+ω})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+ω})|x|}, \] whereas for $ω<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $ω>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<ω<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

papers.title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
papers.abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.

papers.title: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements
papers.abstract: Distance based formation control fixes the shape of a robot team but leaves its position and orientation unconstrained. We regulate all three for differential drive robots that have only one absolute position anchor, absolute headings, body frame relative position measurements, and communication with their neighbors. We derive a two layer estimation control scheme directly from optimization. The first half of the result is a set of graph-proximal estimators that reconstruct the centroid, the anchor vector, and the centered coordinates. Exact proximal updates reach consensus in finitely many steps, and a finite number of primal dual iterations leaves a bounded reconstruction error.
