The controller combines proximal centroid and orientation steps with distance gradient shape regulation, and a finite rotation removes the orientation drift caused by the shape step. A discrete Lyapunov analysis gives local exponential convergence once the estimators have converged. We validate the method in ROS 2 Gazebo and in experiments with five physical robots.

papers.title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
papers.abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. Classical approaches fail along three distinct axes: Kalman-based methods assume Gaussian posteriors and produce biased estimates under nonlinear observation operators; particle-based methods represent distributions with weighted samples and collapse in high dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality; and kernel-based methods move beyond discrete particle representations but cannot maintain their density approximation affordably as dimension grows. The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) avoids all three constraints by encoding the filtering density in a score function and approximating that score with a training-free Monte Carlo estimator, enabling stable filtering in high-dimensional, chaotic systems. This survey traces EnSF's mathematical foundations, establishes it as the state of the art for non-Gaussian, high-dimensional filtering, and examines fourteen extensions that expand its operational reach. Twelve of the fourteen extensions preserve this training-free Monte Carlo estimator at the core of the update, with only two departing from it to achieve planetary-scale deployment.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global Hölder regularity
papers.abstract: Let $ C_ω$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $ω\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_ω$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $β^+>0>β^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $β^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/β^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-Δ_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_ω$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global Hölder regularity for $(-Δ_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible Hölder exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.

papers.title: A Christov Integrating Factor Method for Approximating Rational PDE Solutions
papers.abstract: Rational solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are notoriously difficult to approximate via spectral Fourier methods due to their algebraically slow decay rate. In this work we discuss approximating rational PDE solutions in a basis of orthogonal functions known as the Christov functions, allowing for the computation of its spectrum via the fast Fourier transform. An explicit fourth-order integrating factor method is derived. The effectiveness of the method is tested on several nonlinear PDEs. Relative to a straightforward pseudo-spectral approximation, the integrating factor method supports larger regions of stability resulting in a more efficient scheme.

papers.title: On Submanifolds with constant Möbius Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: In the Möbius geometry of submanifolds there exists an important Möbius invariant tensor called the Möbius metric which together with the Möbius second fundamental form, the Blaschke tensor and the Möbius form constitute a complete system of conformal invariants for umbilic-free submanifolds when the dimension $n \geq 3$. An umbilic-free immersion $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is said to have constant Möbius Ricci curvature if its Möbius metric has constant Ricci curvature. In this paper, we classify umbilic-free immersions $f:M^{n}\to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ with constant Möbius Ricci curvature, flat normal bundle and two distinct principal normal vector fields. We prove that a submanifold with constant Möbius Ricci curvature and flat normal bundle has closed Möbius form, and then we classify such submanifolds provided the Möbius form vanishes identically on $M^{n}$.

papers.title: Isospectral Deformations of Diagonal Matrices by Symmetric Matrices in Dimension Four
papers.abstract: For a diagonal matrix $D$ with distinct diagonal entries in an algebraically closed field $K$ we study the symmetric matrices $Q$ with entries in $K$ such that the affine line $D+tQ$ has the same eigenvalues in $K$ as $D$. We study the equality of characteristic polynomials, $χ_{D+tQ}(x)=χ_D(x) \text{ for all }\: t\in K$ and examine the resulting system of equations. For generic diagonal matrices of size at most $4$ we show that only the trivial symmetric matrix $Q=0$ satisfies this isospectral condition. We use this result to compute the degree of a field extension that appears in the invariant theory of quadratic forms under congruence action.

papers.title: An improved bound for the intersection of two longest cycles in $k$-connected graphs
papers.abstract: A conjecture attributed to Smith states that in every $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest cycles intersects in at least $k$ vertices. We prove that every two longest cycles in a $k$-connected graph on $n$ vertices intersect in at least $\min\{k,10k-n-30\}$ vertices. Consequently, Smith's conjecture holds whenever $k\ge \frac{n+30}{9}$. This improves the previous bound of $\frac{n+16}{7}$ for $n>33$ and also implies a bound of $\frac{n+22}{9}$ for paths instead of cycles.

papers.title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
papers.abstract: We introduce dithered belief-propagation decoding for circuit-level quantum memory to mitigate the oscillations and trapping behavior that limit standard belief-propagation (BP) decoders for qLDPC codes. Our approach combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation. Evaluated under circuit-level noise on the distance-11 rotated surface code and the distance-12 bivariate-bicycle code, the proposed dithered decoder significantly outperforms BP and BP+OSD+CS-10. The proposed decoder achieves accuracy comparable to or better than state-of-the-art Relay-BP, especially at higher physical error rates, while trading a moderate increase in additions for about 98% fewer multiplications on average and eliminating node-level RNGs. These results suggest that dithering is a promising approach toward real-time decoding of quantum memories.

papers.title: Metallic Circles: Concyclic Tangency Points of Ford Circles over $k$-Fibonacci Quotients
papers.abstract: Extending a result of Kocik, we show that the tangency points of the Ford circles built over quotients of $k$-Fibonacci numbers are concyclic: they lie on a circle centred on the horizontal axis, of radius $\sqrt{k^2+4}/2$, meeting it at the reciprocal of the metallic ratio $σ_k$ and at $-σ_k$. Concyclicity turns out to be a quadratic identity of the sequence read in coordinates. In the Poincaré half-plane, this circle is a geodesic along which the tangency points advance with constant step $2\lnσ_k$.

papers.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
papers.abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $Λ$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $Λ$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.

papers.title: Improving the accuracy of the momentum-exchange method in lattice Boltzmann methods
papers.abstract: In the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), the momentum-exchange method (MEM) is widely used to evaluate hydrodynamic forces at fluid-solid interfaces due to its computational efficiency and geometric flexibility. However, when mapping complex geometries onto structured Cartesian grids, the physical boundary rarely intersects the lattice links exactly at their midpoints. This discrepancy violates an implicit assumption inherent to the conventional momentum-exchange (CME) formulation. In this study, we systematically analyze this geometric deficiency and demonstrate that it induces significant force inaccuracies, even in elementary flows where the solid boundary deviates from the midway position. To resolve this, we propose a modified momentum-exchange (MME) method that explicitly accounts for the exact boundary location along the lattice links, demonstrating enhanced accuracy for both flat and curved geometries. Furthermore, we address another critical issue with the interpolation-supplemented bounce-back (ISBB) schemes, and that is their inherent violation of local mass conservation. This mass leakage induces unphysical pressure buildup in the system, which compromises the accuracy and stability of the LBM. We propose a mass-conservative remedy for ISBB schemes that eliminates this leakage. Through a series of benchmark simulations of increasing complexity, we demonstrate that combining the proposed MME with the mass-corrected ISBB scheme drastically improves the fidelity of hydrodynamic force evaluations, establishing a robust framework essential for moving boundary problems and fluid-structure interactions.

papers.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
papers.abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $ζ(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $Δ_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $κ_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $κ_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-χr$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $χ$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $κ$.

papers.title: Perfect Partitions of Regular Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $I_{n,n}$ be a fixed perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, and let $L_{n,1}=K_{n,n}-I_{n,n}$. A perfect set of $L_{n,1}$ is a $1$-factorization of $L_{n,1}$, that is, a set of $n-1$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings whose union is $E(L_{n,1})$; a perfect partition of $L_{n,1}$ is a partition of the set of all perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ into perfect sets. Brualdi, Chiang, and Li (2005) asked whether $L_{n,1}$ admits a perfect partition. Identifying both sides of the bipartition with $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots ,n\}$, the perfect matchings of $L_{n,1}$ are exactly the derangements of $[n]$, the perfect sets correspond bijectively to the reduced Latin squares of order $n$, and the perfect partitions are exactly the perfect matchings of the $(n-1)$-uniform hypergraph whose vertices are the derangements of $[n]$ and whose edges are the perfect sets. We first give, for every $n$, a constructive lower bound on the maximum number of pairwise disjoint perfect sets of $L_{n,1}$. We then show that $L_{5,1}$ has exactly $42$ distinct perfect partitions and that $L_{6,1}$ has at least $82$ distinct perfect partitions; these are the first examples demonstrating that perfect partitions need not be unique. Finally, we exhibit two distinct perfect partitions of $L_{7,1}$, resolving the $n=7$ open problem raised by Brualdi et al.

papers.title: An improved lower bound for maximal partial Room squares
papers.abstract: We establish a new asymptotic lower bound for the volume of a maximal partial Room square of even order $n$. We prove that its volume is at least $\frac{2\sqrt{66}-6}{57}n^2-O(n)$, improving the leading coefficient $1/8$ in the lower bound obtained by Meszka and Rosa. The proof combines two counting arguments, one based on a transversal of empty cells and the other on the graph of occurring symbol pairs.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
papers.abstract: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench response fades, giving a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.

papers.title: Practical Semialgebraic Optimization via Sparse Sample-Based Sum-of-Squares Programming
papers.abstract: As the importance of semialgebraic optimization grows in engineering, so does the need for scalable sum-of-squares (SOS) methods. Their convex relaxations can guide mixed-integer search and often deliver certified global optima outright. Scaling traditional SOS typically requires hand-crafted bases and redundant constraints, whereas sample-based SOS numerically exploits feasible set geometry to reduce bases and build smaller, often tighter relaxations from black-box evaluations. However, discrete variables can require exponentially many samples, and each sampled equation couples all cliques, destroying correlative sparsity. In this work, we avoid enumeration and slack variables by sampling a tractable variety that contains the feasible set, with multipliers only for the omitted constraints. To recover sparsity, we introduce "separator" polynomials that split the sampled equations into local systems coupled only on clique overlaps. This yields a novel, convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs (SDPs) with block sizes and sample requirements governed by local interactions rather than total problem size. Lastly, we show how to verify sample sufficiency and prune redundant equations numerically before solving. In robust estimation and motion planning, we obtain certifiably small optimality gaps at scales far beyond those reported for traditional sparse SOS. For example, we solve a truncated least-squares 3D registration problem with 1600 candidate correspondences in under 49 seconds using an off-the-shelf SDP solver on a laptop CPU.

papers.title: A physics-based adaptive low-rank method for 6D Vlasov simulations
papers.abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank $r$ objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.

papers.title: A second eigenvalue lower bound for the directed configuration model
papers.abstract: We prove a high-probability lower bound for the second eigenvalue in modulus of the transition matrix of the simple random walk on a directed configuration model with minimal out-degree at least two and maximal degree not too large. The lower bound matches the upper bound found by Coste (2021) on the same model. Our proof bypasses the need to establish convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution. Instead, it reduces the spectral lower bound to a central limit theorem for the trace of the transition matrix at powers much larger than the logarithmic scale, a range that previous results failed to reach. Both the general strategy and the central limit theorem might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum subspace methods construct a small subspace from measured basis states and solve the target problem classically within it. We study these methods for heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where the anisotropy $χ_\parallel/χ_\perp$ reaches $10^8$ to $10^{10}$. We prove two results for the energy-norm Galerkin solution. First, if the measurement basis is aligned with the flux surfaces and the subspace contains the poloidal-mode-zero block, the error is bounded by $\|r_0\|_{L^+}(χ_\parallel-χ_\perp)^{-1/2}$, where the numerator does not depend on $χ_\parallel$. The bound is sharp, so the accuracy improves as the anisotropy grows. Second, in the computational basis, a subspace that misses a single node of a flux surface suppresses the flux-function component there as $χ_\parallel^{-1/2}$, which gives an error floor when the limiting solution is nonzero on that surface. We verify both results on a shaped cross-section and on a KSTAR-like Miller equilibrium with ten qubits. At $χ_\parallel/χ_\perp=10^9$, the computational basis gives an error of order unity for every shot budget, whereas a quantum Fourier transform on the poloidal register gives $1.3\times10^{-5}$. The same barrier limits sample-based quantum diagonalization. The aligned measurement needs no time evolution, so the circuit is only state preparation and a five-qubit quantum Fourier transform. On a ten-qubit superconducting processor, the aligned basis gives a median error of $7.0\times10^{-6}$ with 768 shots, whereas the computational basis gives errors above 0.94 up to $1.2\times10^4$ shots. A trapped-ion processor shows the same behavior.

papers.title: An axiom of unique reflection
papers.abstract: We characterize neutral planes by three metric conditions: existence of geodesics, side-side-side congruence, and uniqueness of reflection.

papers.title: Non-Kähler Hyperbolicity: Surfaces and Codimension One
papers.abstract: We study hyperbolicity notions for compact complex manifolds defined by special Hermitian metrics and by holomorphic maps from $\mathbb C^{n-1}$ (divisorial hyperbolicity). For surfaces we show that divisorial and Brody hyperbolicity coincide and that Hermitian-symplectic and Kähler hyperbolicity coincide when $h^{2,0}=0$. In any dimension we prove obstructions to Gauduchon hyperbolicity, show that projective spaces are not divisorially hyperbolic, and give divisorially hyperbolic manifolds that are not balanced hyperbolic.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.

papers.title: Higher theta lifts via BGG resolutions
papers.abstract: We compute higher theta lifts of ladder representations of general linear groups over division algebras over non-archimedean local fields. We achieve this by constructing BGG-type coresolutions and proving that their terms are acyclic for the covariant theta functor. We then compute the resulting complex explicitly, determining the higher theta lifts and the degrees in which they are nonzero.

papers.title: The square function estimates for cones in arbitrary dimensions and elliptic quadrics
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the square function estimate for the light cone in $\R^d$, $d\ge3$, at the exponent $p=2(d-1)/(d-2)$, with loss $[\log(2R)]^{5/p}$ can be deduced from local-smoothing and auxiliary-energy statements in the October 25, 2026 OpenAI manuscript. Exact affine sections preserve these logarithmic bounds and give corresponding estimates for spheres, ellipsoids, elliptic paraboloids, and compact patches of two-sheet elliptic hyperboloids in $\R^{d-1}$.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
papers.abstract: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate comparable to a positive function of the scalar coordinate. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.

papers.title: Seeking the dense half in $K_4$-free graphs
papers.abstract: We show that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a balanced bipartition such that neither part contains more than $0.0671n^2 + o(n^2)$ edges. This improves the previous best bound of $0.074n^2$ by Xu and Zhang. We also formulate a conjecture that the tight bound for this problem is $\frac{425}{6498}n^2 \approx 0.0654n^2$, and present a construction showing that it would be best possible.

papers.title: Ramification of Weighted Central Paths and Super-linear Interior-Point Methods for Semi-definite Optimization
papers.abstract: The local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization is closely tied to the regularity of the central path at its limiting point. Without strict complementarity, the central path can exhibit fractional power asymptotics and need not be differentiable in the ordinary barrier parameter. We show that this obstruction can be removed simultaneously for a family of weighted \AHO~central paths. More precisely, there exists a common ramification exponent $N$ such that all weighted paths in a fixed neighborhood of the identity become analytic at the limiting point after the reparametrization $μ\mapstoμ^N$. Using higher-order derivatives of these reparametrized paths, we construct a feasible $p$th-order predictor-corrector interior-point method. Under a uniform predictor regularity condition, and without assuming strict complementarity, we prove that the normalized complementarity gaps converge with $Q$-order at least $(p+1)/ρ$, where $ρ$ is the reparametrization exponent used by the method. We also establish super-linear convergence of the simultaneously vanishing primal-dual blocks, derive an explicit quantitative reduction bound throughout the predictor regularity region, and obtain a doubly logarithmic outer iteration bound once the iterates enter the local super-linear regime. Finally, we illustrate the predicted higher-order behavior on a collection of degenerate and non-degenerate semi-definite optimization problems.

papers.title: The odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$
papers.abstract: We introduce a class of interesting algebraic varieties --- odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k,2n+1)$ and study them with an emphasis on the case of the submaximal odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(n,2n+1)$, which we call catalecticant varieties. The main result of the paper is a construction of a full exceptional collection in the derived category of the catalecticant sixfold $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$.

papers.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
papers.abstract: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^α$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^γ_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $α+ 2γ< 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.

papers.title: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
papers.abstract: Advanced LIGO is a gravitational-wave detector with extreme sensitivity, operating close to the quantum limits of optical measurement. The quantum noise in this system arises from vacuum fluctuations entering the interferometer readout port: phase-like fluctuations produce measurement imprecision, while amplitude-like fluctuations drive radiation-pressure back-action. In this review, we present an intuitive description in terms of complex fields and quadratures, and follow squeezed vacuum from its generation, through its interaction with the filter cavity and propagation through the interferometer, to the readout. We discuss how frequency-independent and frequency-dependent squeezing engineer quantum noise, and how correlations between optical quadratures map onto correlations between measurement imprecision and back-action. We conclude that LIGO is both a gravitational-wave observatory and a kilometre-scale platform for quantum measurement science.

papers.title: Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell
papers.abstract: We construct a model for the response of a detector to vacuum fluctuations inside a massive hollow shell in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass gives rise to a superposition of spacetime geometries and their associated vacuum fluctuations. To describe this system, we employ the formalism of quantum reference frames to transition to a frame in which the source mass occupies a definite position while the detector is in a superposition of positions. This allows the dynamics of the detector to be analyzed using standard tools of quantum field theory on a definite curved spacetime. We compute the detector response for a wide range of configurations of the shell and detector positions and investigate how information about the quantum state of the shell is encoded in the response function, identifying features of the superposition that are effectively captured by the detector. In particular, we show that, under appropriate postselection, the response function exhibits interference patterns, and identify regions of the parameter space of the model in which the shell-induced contributions to the interference terms are maximized.

papers.title: Compatible Hamel Topologies, Real Valued Isomorphisms and Rational Scalar Continuity
papers.abstract: We study Hamel character topologies on the real line in two parts. Part I treats the full real-orbit (TVG) and the rational-parameter (TVGQ) dual pairs. A divisibility-chain criterion decides compatibility on the rationals and on Q/Z. Compatible subsets of one chain have a compatible join, but two different chains need not: an explicit Chinese remainder construction gives two compatible topologies with an incompatible join. This answers the compact-union question negatively, disproves the Greatest Compatible TVG Conjecture for every nonzero rational-valued Hamel functional, and shows that the corresponding rational and real dual pairs admit no Mackey topology. We classify additive homomorphisms and isomorphisms of the real-valued observation spaces and their automorphism groups, prove that both prime square-denominator topologies are non-nuclear, classify sequences converging for every coefficient functional, and show that the real parameters of continuous characters of the integers with the mixed-prime metric form a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Part II studies real vector spaces whose Hausdorff additive group topology makes every fixed rational scalar multiplication continuous (TVGQ). A rational-valued Hamel functional and a rational parameter space S generate precompact, modular and real-valued observation topologies whose exact scalar ring is the multiplier ring of S. We compute their completions and character groups, classify the precompact TVGQ topologies, characterize universal separating sequences, show that local compactness and sigma-compactness force the scalar ring to be a field, classify isomorphisms within each modular family (exactly 2^c types), identify greatest-compatible existence with the unrestricted Mackey problem, and prove that all compatible topologies for the rational Hamel pair are non-Baire.

papers.title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
papers.abstract: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations. This tilting-bundle method also allows us to lift the construction from derived to homotopy categories of complexes of modules, reducing the calculation of tangle invariants to a type of categorified matrix algebra, where the matrices in question have maps between their elements and calculations get turbocharged with chain homotopy.

papers.title: Coherent detector responses to quantum-controlled spherical-shell geometries
papers.abstract: A detector inside a static spherical shell samples globally matched field modes even though its local geometry is flat. We construct the response of a compactly switched Unruh-DeWitt detector on a quantum-controlled pair of transparent spherical-shell spacetimes with common Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass. A stipulated common-incoming scattering identification places the branch excitations in one Hilbert space. Their positive Gram matrix determines joint, conditional, and dephased detector responses at a finite common readout, retaining the physical detector-clock phase in the uncompensated protocol. An additional coherent phase-gate protocol compensates free detector-clock propagation while preserving the shell interaction response. For concentric shells the centered response is exactly $s$ wave. A common incoming direction basis extends the construction to a lab-fixed detector and displaced shell centers, preserving common-translation covariance. The equal-radius benchmark exhibits conditional changes of order $25\%$ without dark-port amplification. Combining radius and position produces an assignment-odd response that reverses under reflection and vanishes at the relational midpoint. The relative normalized-state contrast reaches $34.15\%$ among the computed samples; the relative clock-resolved probe-influence contrast reaches $8.09\%$ for the declared readout, while larger values belong to its separate shared-phase envelope. These effects already occur in the dominant-energy-condition-compatible core. They are relational, model-dependent detector responses, not a background-independent witness of quantum geometry. First-order coefficients have finite pointlike limits; finite-coupling statements are made only at a fixed shared regulator.

papers.title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase π/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.

papers.title: Agnostic and efficient detection of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry-protected topological phases in projected entangled-pair states
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are the simplest example of quantum phases that cannot be detected by local order parameters. Their classification is by now well-established from multiple perspectives, a prominent one being via tensor network states. The practical question, however, is not mere classification, but detection: given the ground state of an interacting Hamiltonian and a symmetry group $G$ along with its representation, is there an efficient way to tell if the state is in a SPT phase with respect to $G$? While there exist such practical tests in one spatial dimension (1D), methods in 2D have so far been restricted to finite-size systems or require an explicit form of virtual symmetries of the tensor networks representing the ground state. Here, we develop an agnostic and efficient method to detect interacting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 2D SPT phases, using an infinite projected entangled-pair (PEPS) representation of the ground state. The method is agnostic to the symmetry representation in the virtual space of the PEPS tensor and applicable independent of the bond dimension of the tensors. Moreover, it is efficient as it does not require finite-size scalings: it works directly in the thermodynamic limit. We numerically demonstrate the procedure by mapping out phase boundaries away from fixed-point wavefunctions. We extract the SPT label cocycle data explicitly from the PEPS tensor.

papers.title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability $p\in[0,1]$. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to $Sp(N)$ rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for $N\ge40$, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of $Sp(N)$ under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including $SU(N)$.

papers.title: Constraint Variance Identity and the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation
papers.abstract: The quantum Hamiltonian constraint vanishes for physical states. For separable Hamiltonians in minisuperspace, its vanishing variance yields a fundamental identity. Under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we derive the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation, dynamically linking spacetime clock fluctuations to matter fluctuations. This establishes a quantitative stability condition for the clock against total quantum noise. Finally, we obtain an uncertainty relation between matter energy and relational time. The stable existence of spacetime thus demands quantum fluctuations in matter.

papers.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
papers.abstract: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.

papers.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
papers.abstract: We prove a lower bound of $Ω_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusnády's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors.

papers.title: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs
papers.abstract: Resource analyses for quantum programs commonly provide safe upper bounds on qubits, gates, or non-Clifford operations. We study a single-qubit dyadic fragment in which the deepest exact resource layer can instead be inferred exactly. Starting from the normalized-midpoint misty-state syntax, we define dyadic program states and the real cyclotomic tower $K_D=\mathbb Q(2\cos(π/2^D))$. For the projective single-qubit Clifford-cyclotomic tower $\widehat G_D\subseteq SO(3)$, we prove the relative intersection law $\widehat G_D\cap SO(3,K_d)=\widehat G_d$ for $d\le D$. Combining this descent theorem with an arithmetic-closure invariant for adaptive stabilizer processing yields $\mathrm{Fdepth}(U)=\mathrm{Adepth}(U)=\mathrm{Rdepth}(U)$: the smallest real cyclotomic field containing the Bloch matrix of an exactly synthesizable channel, the shallowest dyadic gate alphabet realizing it up to global phase, and the shallowest dyadic program-state layer sufficient for exact stabilizer-assisted implementation coincide. At that common minimum, known fixed-alphabet synthesis gives minimum primitive-rotation count. We package the result as an exact static resource effect and outline a certificate-producing compiler.

papers.title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
papers.abstract: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.

papers.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
papers.abstract: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^γ$, where $γ\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $γ$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

papers.title: Lifts of Brauer characters and vertex pairs for odd primes
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group, and let $\varphi\in\IBr_p(G)$ have vertex $Q$. We prove that $\varphi$ has at most $|Q:Q'|$ lifts to ordinary irreducible characters, establishing Cossey's conjecture for odd primes.

papers.title: 3D Printed Monolithic Optomechanical Chassis for an Unbalanced Field-Widened Interferometer
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing is increasingly being explored as an approach for producing complex structures for optical hardware. In this work, we present a fully monolithic optomechanical chassis fabricated using laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. The structure was fabricated from thermally stable Invar36, a low-thermal-expansion alloy that enables high dimensional stability under varying environmental conditions. Our monolithic design incorporates embedded optical mounts, flexures, and alignment features directly into the chassis geometry that exceed the practical limits of conventional subtractive manufacturing. By integrating the optomechanical support structure into a single compact unit, the system achieves a reduced footprint compared to traditional optomechanical assemblies. The results demonstrate the potential of additive manufacturing to produce lightweight, and highly customized optical systems, opening the possibility of new pathways for next-generation quantum sensors and optical instrumentation.

papers.title: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
papers.abstract: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.

papers.title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
papers.abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Ripà and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.

papers.title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
papers.abstract: The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $nρ_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $nρ_n^{2+β}\to0$, where $ρ_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+β$ moments for some $β>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.

papers.title: $ω$-limit sets of triangular maps over periodic orbits of the base
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f(x),g(x,y))$ be a continuous triangular map of the unit square and let $z=(x_0,y_0)$ be a point such that $ω_f(x_0)$ is a periodic orbit $\{p_0,\dots,p_{m-1}\}$ of $f$. Then $ω_F(z)=\bigcup_{i}\{p_i\}\times M_i$ for nonempty compact sets $M_i$, and we ask which $m$-tuples $(M_0,\dots,M_{m-1})$ occur. For $m=1$ the answer is a theorem of Kolyada and Snoha. We show that a tuple occurs if and only if there are continuous surjections $M_i\to M_{i+1}$, indices modulo $m$, whose composition around the cycle is chain transitive. This is a cyclic version of classical facts due to Dowker and Friedlander, Sharkovsky, Hirsch, Smith and Zhao, and Kolyada and Snoha. It yields two necessary conditions: no $M_i$ is one of the exceptional sets of Kolyada and Snoha, and there are continuous surjections $M_0\to M_1\to\dots\to M_{m-1}\to M_0$. We prove that these conditions are also sufficient when every $M_i$ has uncountably many connected components, and when every $M_i$ has countably many components of which only finitely many are nondegenerate. In particular the sections of one $ω$-limit set need not be homeomorphic. Every tuple satisfying the two conditions falls into one of these cases or into a single remaining class, in which the sections have countably many components and infinitely many of them are nondegenerate; that class is studied in a companion paper.

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Stochastic Optimal Control on Positive Cones
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic optimal control problems in which the state is constrained to a proper cone. Specifically, we consider risk-neutral, risk-averse, and risk-seeking formulations within a single entropic-risk framework. We investigate classes of problems whose Bellman operator preserves affine functions and characterize their optimal value functions and feedback policies for both finite-horizon and time-average infinite-horizon problems. Additionally, we establish convergence and state-bound results under finite-step cost observability. Moreover, we demonstrate an exact connection between entropic-risk optimal control on proper cones and deterministic infsup control for systems whose dynamics and stage costs are affine in the disturbances. In addition, we provide examples of classes of systems for which explicit solutions can be obtained.

papers.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
papers.abstract: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq v(H)^{Cv(F)^2}$$ for all graphs $F$ and $H$. The proof combines a variant of a random geometric construction of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl with the hypergraph container method.

papers.title: On Natural Exponential Families with Log-Affine Generalized Variance
papers.abstract: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat Kähler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi Mode: Budget-Aware Routing of Optimizers By Online Landscape Probes
papers.abstract: The best classical optimizer for a continuous black-box problem depends on its budget and landscape. Existing routers decide from the dimension and budget, past improvement or features fitted to one benchmark, and few test an optimizer's implicit assumptions online. AMM (Adaptive Multi Mode) routes a known budget among quasi-Newton, trust-region, coordinate, multistart and evolution-strategy optimization engines with online probes of curvature, plateaus, separability, kinks, basins and fractal structure. Each probe has a default, a dimension-by-budget validity range and a cost charged to the budget. In its pre-registered development loop on bbob, 32 of 36 predictions held over the last 16 confirmations. AMM was then tested once on held-out bbob instances 101-110 (D=2-40, 10*D-1000*D) against up to seven competitors. It has the highest target share in 382 of 600 function-dimension-budget cells (236 outright, 146 tied) and, by a descriptive posterior rule, is credibly behind in 35, mostly at 10*D and 30*D. At every budget it also leads the controls built from its own engines (the best engine alone, the best engine per dimension and budget, and a greedy schedule), narrowly at 10*D and 30*D, and nevergrad's NgIohTuned. In pre-registered runs its lead over IPOP-CMA-ES holds under affine and box transformations, on box-constrained bbob and, pooled, on rotated f2-f4, but rotating the separable f3 and f4 removes most of the lead there. On held-out MA-BBOB its final share at 2000*D is level with IPOP-CMA-ES's and its anytime area lower. We published AMM as an open-source Python package (pip install amm-optimizer; https://github.com/BjBodner/amm-optimizer).

papers.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
papers.abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.

papers.title: A property of boundary extensions of atomic singular inner functions
papers.abstract: Using a property of the Hilbert transform, we prove a measure theoretic result concerning the extensions of atomic singular inner functions to the circle. Various alternative proofs are presented using the mean value theorem for harmonic functions and a well-known property of Blaschke products. Using the main result, we establish several facts concerning atomic singular inner functions and their logarithms.

papers.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
papers.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two-dimensional charge-density field. The desired spatial distribution of the confined charge defines the target quantum-dot geometry for inverse design. The FNO reproduces charge densities with a relative $L^2$ test error of just 0.6\% and enables millisecond-scale differentiable evaluations. Relative to the CPU-based physics simulator, the FNO achieves a 17,000-fold speed-up on GPU for a single design, with further performance gains enabled by batched inference. When embedded in a gradient-based design loop with fabrication constraints, the FNO can produce both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions. The ability to engineer these distinct confinement configurations demonstrates control over quantum-dot shape and position, providing a route towards designing devices with distinct qubit-relevant operating properties prior to fabrication.

papers.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
papers.abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $Φ(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: The pliability of del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We study $G$-Mori fibre space models of $G$-del Pezzo surfaces, focusing on surfaces over non-closed fields. We construct explicit examples of birationally rigid sextic del Pezzo surfaces and give a negative answer to a generalization of Kollár's question on birational rigidity and field extensions: a sextic del Pezzo surface of Picard rank $1$ can fail to be birationally rigid over its ground field but become birationally rigid after an algebraic field extension. We interpret this phenomenon in terms of the failure of injectivity of natural maps in nonabelian Galois cohomology induced by the inclusion of automorphism groups into birational automorphism groups. We also show that finite pliability is unbounded: for every integer $d\geqslant2$, we construct a sextic del Pezzo surface of index $3$ over a field of characteristic zero whose pliability is exactly $3^d+1$.

papers.title: Largest Sperner families with bounded VC-dimension
papers.abstract: A conjecture of Frankl proposed in the 1980s states that for $n\ge2d$, every Sperner family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ of VC-dimension at most $d$ has at most $\binom{n}{d}$ members. We prove this conjecture for every fixed $d$ and large $n$, and show that equality holds only when $\mathcal{F}$ is $\binom{[n]}{d}$ or $\binom{[n]}{n-d}$.

papers.title: Deterministic Fault-Tolerant Connectivity Oracles with Subquadratic Space
papers.abstract: A fault-tolerant (FT) connectivity oracle for an $n$-vertex graph $G=(V,E)$ determines whether $G- F$ is connected for any query set $F\subseteq E$. When the number of failures is unrestricted, prior constructions exhibited a sharp contrast between randomization and determinism: randomized oracles use only $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space [Duan and Pettie, SICOMP 2020], whereas no deterministic construction was known to improve upon storing $G$ explicitly, requiring $Θ(n^2)$ bits in the worst case. The promise that $F\subseteq E$ is essential for subquadratic space: allowing arbitrary queries $F\subseteq V\times V$ forces quadratic space. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, Khanna, Konrad, and Putterman [SODA 2027] recently constructed deterministic oracles using $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{f}n)$ space that also report approximate distances with polylogarithmic stretch. Their result improves upon the classical $O(fn)$ space bound for deterministic connectivity oracles [Pătraşcu and Thorup, FOCS 2007], but offers no space savings over storing $G$ when $f=Θ(n^2)$. We present the first deterministic connectivity oracles with subquadratic space for failure sets of unrestricted size, using $\widetilde{O}(n^{7/4})$ space. We also establish the first polynomial separation between deterministic and randomized connectivity oracles, proving that every deterministic oracle requires $\widetildeΩ(n^{3/2})$ bits in the worst case. For queries containing at most $f$ failures, we obtain deterministic connectivity oracles using $\widetilde{O}(f^{2/5}n)$ space, improving the dependence on $f$ in the bound of Khanna et al., and prove a lower bound of $\widetildeΩ(f^{1/4}n)$ bits.

papers.title: Hessenberg character
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.

papers.title: Morphisms of $A_\infty$-algebras and modules
papers.abstract: $A_\infty$-algebra is a chain complex equipped with a coherent multiplicative structure, i.e. a multiplication which is commutative up to (higher) chain homotopy. Similarly $A_\infty$-module over such algebra is equipped with its coherent action. These notions are used to represent cohomological information contained in topological multiplicative structures. One of the key tools of the theory are minimal models, which are useful in cohomological computations. In this thesis author presents certain sufficient conditions for a morphism of $A_\infty$-modules to induce a morphism of their minimal models.

papers.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
papers.abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.

papers.title: Delay-induced multirhythmicity in a 3-cell inhibitory network
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of a delayed three-cell central pattern generator network using return-map analysis and a phase-reduced description derived from generalized FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators. The phase model captures the emergence and stability of synchronous, pacemaker, and traveling-wave rhythms and provides a systematic, computationally efficient framework for characterizing the network dynamics beyond direct return-map calculations. We conduct extensive two-parameter analyses of both the full and phase-reduced models, revealing rich multi-rhythmic dynamics and transitions among coexisting rhythmic states. The close agreement between the two descriptions establishes phase reduction as an efficient and reliable framework for characterizing the dynamical organization of delayed neural oscillator networks.

papers.title: Independent Backward Preimages and Algebraic Radial Decompositions of Operators
papers.abstract: Let $T\in\mathcal{B}(X)$, where $X$ is a complex Banach space. We introduce the spaces $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$, defined by independently chosen preimages under the powers of $T$ with exponential growth bounds, and study algebraic radial decompositions involving $\mathcal{H}_r(T)$, $\mathcal{K}_s(T)$, and $\mathcal{I}_s(T)$. We prove that every algebraic decomposition $X=\mathcal{H}_r(T)\oplus\mathcal{I}_s(T)$ is topological and that $\mathcal{I}_s(T)=\mathcal{K}_s(T)$. This removes the closedness assumption in the radial decomposition theorem of Koliha and Poon. We also prove that, for $0\leq a\leq b$, the closedness of $\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ and $\mathcal{H}_a(T)+\mathcal{I}_b(T)$ implies $\mathcal{I}_b(T)=\mathcal{K}_b(T)$. We establish finite-defect and circular spectral criteria and characterize the Cantor--Bendixson derivatives of the spectrum, Browder spectrum, and Drazin spectrum in terms of radial decompositions and quotient restrictions. As applications, we obtain new characterizations of generalized Drazin, generalized Drazin--Riesz, generalized Drazin--meromorphic, and $g_z$-invertible operators in terms of radial subspaces.

papers.title: Spectral and mapping properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator
papers.abstract: We investigate the spectral and boundedness properties of the inverse Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$ and its associated semigroup in $L^p$ spaces with respect to the inverse Gaussian measure. We establish strong continuity and contractivity of this semigroup in $L^p$ for $p \in [1, \infty)$, and obtain a complete characterization of the spectrum of $\mathcal{A}^{Q,B}$. For $p \in (1, \infty)$, the spectrum is independent of $p$, consists entirely of eigenvalues and exhibits a spectral gap. For $p=1$, the spectrum is instead the left half-plane. Furthermore, we discuss ultracontractivity and hypercontractivity properties of the semigroup.

papers.title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
papers.abstract: Data arising in scientific applications often exhibits complex nonlinear structure. Identifying and parameterizing said nonlinearities can enable better modeling, enhance predictive analysis, data interpolation, denoising, and anomaly detection. In this paper, we develop theoretical and computational methods to detect and parametrize Euclidean point cloud data lying near a wedge sum of tori. Specifically, we use persistent cohomology and cup products to identify the distinct toroidal components, and on each component, we optimize over low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials for best data fit. The ensuing optimization problem reduces to generalized ridge regression, which can be solved efficiently via standard techniques. We demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in both synthetic and real datasets, including interpolation of low frame-rate recurrent videos, attractor recovery in quasiperiodic dynamical systems, and the parametrization of gene-space cycle data for parasites and humans.

papers.title: On isospectral potentials on periodic discrete graphs
papers.abstract: We consider discrete Schrödinger operators with periodic (possibly complex valued) potentials $Q$ on periodic graphs. Using a system of spectral invariants obtained in \cite{S26}, we investigate the sets of isospectral potentials on periodic graphs. In particular, we show that the Floquet spectrum of the Schrödinger operators on the hexagonal lattice and on the Kagome lattice generically (with respect to perturbations of $Q$) determines the potential $Q$ uniquely up to the obvious symmetries (translations and rotations) in the periodic graph.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Response Functions: Resolvent Kernels, Time-Domain Sampling, Query Lower Bounds with Matched Single-Point Calibers, and a Six-Route Comparison
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for molecular response functions have mostly been studied one route at a time, most prominently the indicator-binning algorithm of Kharazi et al. We compare six routes within one accounting framework and state the conversions between their resource calibers. On the resolvent route the Lorentz-broadened spectrum is exactly a resolvent expectation; at finite gamma two boundary terms, a reversal term and a permanent-dipole pseudo-line, enter a disjoint error budget. Because the kernel subnormalization is exactly 1, the published binning accounting carries a removable Theta(alpha+1+omega) factor (49.69x and 7.75x at the definitional caliber), a correction that applies to both routes. Estimating the square root of the kernel amplitude lowers the readout cost from beta^2/mu_tilde_2 to beta/sqrt(mu_tilde_2). On the time-domain route we prove a single-point amplitude-estimation theorem and convert the generalized QPE of Loaiza et al. to the same accounting. The lower bounds are Theta_tilde(1/gamma) for parameter location, Theta(1/(gamma epsilon)) for windowed values, Omega(n/gamma) inside a restricted correlation-sampling class, and Omega(1/(epsilon gamma^2)) on the Lorentzian object; in the single-circuit-resolution caliber, gamma^(-n) is a grid-coverage artifact. Six routes, their calibers, an n=2 assembly with a component-grade coherence, and a phase diagram over the tested ensembles form one accounting map.

papers.title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: Choosing a quantum error-correcting code for a real device means scoring candidates with circuit-level simulations so slow that only a few hundred can be run. So every evaluation counts, and a search is judged by how many good codes it finds per paid evaluation. Quantum LDPC codes built from a few group elements protect many logical qubits, but good ones are rare in a huge space. We introduce GFlowQEC, to our knowledge the first generative flow network (GFlowNet) for quantum code design. It builds a code one group element at a time and learns to propose codes in proportion to a power of their score. We train it once on scores from earlier searches, freeze it, and let it propose lifted-product codes with 180 physical qubits, scored by their distances. Ranking ten of its draws per paid call, it finds more than twice as many new top-scoring codes (inequivalent to any it was trained on) as tuned parallel tempering, even when tempering starts from GFlowQEC's training codes. It finds more than three and a half times as many as a supervised screen ranking ten random candidates per call. When both rank a hundred, the screen beats GFlowQEC, and does best ranking GFlowQEC's draws. Soft Q-learning, which shares the GFlowNet's optimal policy, does as well at one noise bias and better at the other, so the gain does not depend on the GFlowNet's training loss. Trained proposers can make a budget of expensive evaluations go further when good codes are rare.

papers.title: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes
